title: The Entropic Markov Model (EMM): System and Method for Predicting Dynamic Outcomes in Human, Organizational, and Socio-Technical Systems

detail.title: The Entropic Markov Model (EMM): System and Method for Predicting Dynamic Outcomes in Human, Organizational, and Socio-Technical Systems
detail.abstract: The Entropic Markov Model (EMM) provides a unified computational framework for analyzing and predicting transitions in complex adaptive systems. By introducing entropy-weighted probabilistic transitions and behavioral-energy coefficients, EMM captures both structural uncertainty and motivational momentum within dynamic environments. The model applies to human, organizational, and socio-technical systems where state changes are influenced by internal energy and disorder. This publication presents the theoretical basis, algorithmic structure, and multi-domain applicability of EMM, including organizational transformation, behavioral analytics, and macro-system forecasting.

detail.title: Understanding the Awareness of Accounting Students on Growing Usage of Fintech in Banking Sector, with Special Reference to Students of CEBA, UTAS
detail.abstract:
The financial services sector, including banking and accounting, is undergoing rapid transformation driven by financial technology (finTech). As finTech reshapes how accounting and finance are practiced, it is essential for accounting students to understand its impact. By introducing automation, enhancing data analytics, and enabling innovative financial products and services, finTech is redefining traditional accounting roles.

FinTech tools such as cloud-based software, artificial intelligence (AI), and robotic process automation are streamlining accounting processes, improving efficiency, and saving time. This shift prepares students for an increasingly automated workforce. Moreover, advanced data analytics and financial reporting capabilities allow professionals to evaluate performance, forecast trends, and make informed decisions—giving accounting graduates a competitive edge.

Blockchain technology further strengthens financial record-keeping by providing secure, transparent, and immutable transaction records. It reduces fraud, ensures regulatory compliance, and supports cryptocurrency management. As digital payment systems, mobile banking, and cryptocurrencies gain traction, accounting students must understand blockchain, manage transactions, and stay current with evolving regulations.

FinTech also enhances risk management and regulatory compliance, reducing manual processes and safeguarding integrity in the banking industry. For accounting students, staying informed about these advancements is critical to remaining relevant and competitive. By mastering digital payments, blockchain, automation, data analytics, and regulatory technologies, they position themselves as tech-savvy professionals capable of meeting the dynamic needs of the financial sector.

Ultimately, the integration of finTech into banking is transforming the role of accounting professionals. Students who embrace these technologies will combine technical expertise with financial acumen, making them adaptable and highly marketable in a digitalized financial world.

title: Social Media Platforms as Shadow Governments: Why Facebook Should Issue Passports

detail.title: Social Media Platforms as Shadow Governments: Why Facebook Should Issue Passports
detail.abstract: This paper argues that large social media platforms have evolved into de facto 'shadow governments,' exercising sovereign-like powers over vast digital populations. Through analysis of platform governance mechanisms, enforcement structures, and economic systems, we demonstrate that these entities perform functions increasingly analogous to those of nationstates: they regulate speech through content moderation policies, enforce community standards via algorithmic and human review systems, manage digital economies worth billions of dollars, and maintain sophisticated internal adjudication processes that rival formal legal systems. We propose a radical but logical next step: that these platforms should begin issuing their own digital passports, thereby formalizing their role as global actors and providing a new framework for digital identity that transcends traditional national boundaries. This proposition, while provocative, forces a necessary reckoning with the locus of power in the digital age and challenges fundamental assumptions about sovereignty, citizenship, and the nation-state in an increasingly networked world. We examine the legal, political, and social implications of this corporate sovereignty framework, arguing that explicit recognition of platform power is preferable to the current regime of implicit governance that operates without democratic accountability or clear jurisdictional boundaries.

detail.title: Strategic Evaluation of Statistical, Machine Learning, and Foundation Models for Forecasting

publicationDetails.detailsText: 35th Annual Workshop on Information Technologies and Systems (WITS’25), Nashville, Tennessee, December 17-19, 2025

detail.abstract: As predictive models become central to platforms like Airbnb, accurately forecasting user behavior is increasingly vital. This study compares the performance of twelve forecasting models—ranging from traditional statistical methods (ARIMA, TSLM) and neural networks (NNETAR) to zero-shot foundation models (ChatGPT-4o, TimeGPT)—using monthly guest review data from Airbnb listings in New York City and Chicago (2016–2024). Reviews serve as a proxy for visitor demand. Results show that traditional models (TSLM in NYC, ARIMA in Chicago) consistently outperform foundation models in RMSE and MAE. Foundation models fail to capture seasonal peaks and sudden shifts, highlighting their limitations in structured forecasting tasks without domain-specific tuning. These findings offer theoretical insight into model generalizability and practical guidance for selecting forecasting tools in platform environments.

title: Pretraining vs. Instruction Tuning in LLMs: A Conceptual Taxonomy, Implications, and Research Frontiers

detail.title: Pretraining vs. Instruction Tuning in LLMs: A Conceptual Taxonomy, Implications, and Research Frontiers
detail.abstract: This research note presents a conceptual summary and analysis of the paper "AI Agents vs. Agentic AI: A Conceptual Taxonomy, Applications and Challenges" arXiv:2505.10468. The authors chart the evolution of LLMs from data-driven pretraining to goal-directed instruction tuning. In this commentary, I highlight the paper's taxonomy, discuss its implications for AI system design, and reflect on current research gaps. This synthesis is intended for both scholars and practitioners aiming to understand the paradigmatic shift in how large language models are trained, aligned, and deployed.

title: Beyond Shannon: Geometric Transformations and the Foundations of Set Shaping Theory

detail.title: Beyond Shannon: Geometric Transformations and the Foundations of Set Shaping Theory
detail.abstract: Set Shaping Theory (SST) proposes a structural reformulation of information theory in which compression efficiency arises not from probabilistic modelling of the source, but from a geometric reshaping of the sequence space itself. Instead of assuming a fixed domain 𝑆𝑁 of sequences of length N, SST introduces bijective transformations f: 𝑆 𝑁 → 𝑆 𝑁+𝑘 whose images occupy deliberately structured subsets of the larger space. These shaped subsets exhibit reduced average empirical entropy, not merely in terms of symbolic frequency, but in the full entropylength product ⟨(N + k)H₀(f(s))⟩ < ⟨N H₀(s)⟩, the universal limit governing coding when the source distribution is unknown. This demonstrates that entropy, classically treated as an intrinsic property of the source, is in fact coordinate-dependent: it varies with the geometric constraints imposed on the combinatorial domain. Consequently, SST enables reductions in the theoretical compression limit, provides inherent self-verification through the exclusion of non-admissible sequences, and unifies structural redundancy, compression, and reliability within a single architectural framework. The theory establishes a new axis in information theory structural efficiency revealing that the geometry of representation can be engineered to outperform modelbased approaches without violating Shannon's bounds. This work positions SST as a foundational extension of classical information theory and outlines its implications for coding theory, algorithmic complexity, symbolic machine learning, and discrete informational geometry.

detail.title: Inward or Outward? Attentional Focus and Trust Formation in the Sharing Economy Platforms

publicationDetails.detailsText: 35th Annual Workshop on Information Technologies and Systems (WITS’25), Nashville, Tennessee, December 17-19, 2025

detail.abstract: This study theorizes and tests how attentional focus in provider's self-disclosure—specifically, self- vs. other-focused language—shapes perceived trustworthiness and economic outcomes on digital sharing economy platforms. Drawing on the Elaboration Likelihood Model and Social Role Theory, we analyze a large dataset with 0.26 million listings from a leading digital sharing economy platform using deep learning and robust regression methods. Results reveal a curvilinear relationship: higher self-focus reduces trustworthiness at an accelerating rate. However, this effect is attenuated for female providers, consistent with gendered trust heuristics. Trust, in turn, predicts higher prices, beyond standard reputation metrics. We introduce attentional focus as a novel, measurable trust signal in IS research. Our study has several theoretical and practical implications.

detail.abstract: We present a compact first-draft specification of the Informational Pixel Field (IPF) framework. The theory is driven by a Master Lagrangian with fundamental pixel scales (ℓP , εP , c) and a scalar informational field ΦI that modulates gauge and matter sectors via the profiles (Z1(ΦI ), Zs(ΦI ), m(ΦI )). We list the field equations, the nine-domain decomposition, pixel principles and capacity triad, proton mass structure, operational constraints, a symbol glossary, and an appendix table mapping domains to observables. This draft includes an explicit Scope & Limitations section (no proofs) to make the current research readiness and boundaries fully transparent.

title: The Mathematical Bridge: Deriving the Causal Prediction Metric (Φ): FluxSense from Adaptive Order from Inherent Flux (AOIF) for Systemic Risk Mitigation

detail.title: The Mathematical Bridge: Deriving the Causal Prediction Metric (Φ): FluxSense from Adaptive Order from Inherent Flux (AOIF) for Systemic Risk Mitigation
detail.abstract: Current models in complex, chaotic systems rely fundamentally on probabilistic risk assessment, which is inherently incapable of guaranteeing pre-emptive, deterministic intervention. This paper introduces the foundational framework that treats informational units as a physical resource subject to measurable kinetic laws. We apply the principles of Adaptive Order from Inherent Flux (AOIF) to derive the Causal Prediction Metric (Φ): FluxSense. This metric is derived from the second-order derivative of the system's structural state, quantifying the kinetic acceleration of informational disorder. Measuring this acceleration is mathematically necessary and sufficient to determine, with deterministic certainty, the exact time window required for a successful intervention (𝒫 𝒞𝒫) before a critical failure state is reached. This work establishes the scientific basis for deterministic stability, fundamentally replacing probabilistic risk models in high-flux, mission-critical environments.

title: Product Failure or Streamer Misconduct? A Study of Brand Crises and Consumer Complaints in Live-Streaming E-Commerce
affiliations: Ocean University of China, Ocean University of China and Wuhan University of Technology

detail.title: Product Failure or Streamer Misconduct? A Study of Brand Crises and Consumer Complaints in Live-Streaming E-Commerce
detail.abstract: In recent years, live streaming e-commerce has become an important channel for the retail industry to promote brands and improve sales performance. With the increasing popularity of live streaming e-commerce, we have also witnessed a large number of brand crises, which significantly damage brand reputation and sales. Drawing on social exchange theory, this study investigates the interaction between brand crisis types (product-related vs. streamer-related) and live streamer types (enterprise-affiliated vs. celebrity) on consumer complaints. By conducting three experimental studies, we find that consumer complaints are more pronounced when a streamer-related crisis caused by an enterprise-affiliated streamer versus a celebrity streamer. However, this effect is mitigated when a product-related crisis occurs. The results reveal that psychological contract breach mediates the interactive effects between crisis types and streamer types on consumer complaints. This study also confirmed that service recovery strategies can serve as effective intervention measures for dealing with brand crises. In celebrity streamer-related crises, emotional remediation mitigates the psychological contract breach, thereby reducing consumer complaints. In product-related crises, economic remediation can reduce consumer complaints by decreasing the psychological contract breach. This study enriches theoretical research on brand crises and extends the practical application of social exchange theory in live-streaming e-commerce. It also offers a theoretical foundation and practical insights for platforms seeking to optimize management strategies in response to consumer negative feedback.

title: From Exclusion to Inclusion: Financial Integration Policies and Socio-Demographic Determinants in Global Ageing Society

detail.title: From Exclusion to Inclusion: Financial Integration Policies and Socio-Demographic Determinants in Global Ageing Society
detail.abstract: As a cornerstone to accelerate the achievement of the 17 SDGs, raising the level of financial inclusion (FI) is essential to ensure that economic growth, employment, empowerment of women, and poverty are well addressed. Despite over 79 percent of adults having formal financial accounts, over 1.3 billion are still excluded from formal financial services, underscoring the need to invest in targeted determinants to improve financial inclusivity of vulnerable populations. Utilizing pooled cross-sectional data from the World Bank’s Global Findex and World Development Indicators databases from 2017 and 2021, a generalized ordered logistic regression model was employed to investigate structural and individual characteristics that drive changes in inclusion levels. The findings reveal that human capital is the most robust determinant. Under population ageing, older adults are more likely to struggle in transitioning to higher inclusion levels. Gender disparity is highly regional-dependent, with females in Sub-Saharan Africa showing lower inclusivity when compared to other regions. Finally, COVID-19 had a strong correlation with inclusivity, highlighting the impact of global financial transformation in the post-pandemic world. The study concludes that prioritizing investment in human capital development will enhance people's awareness, access, and progress towards higher financial inclusivity.

title: Current account and monetary policy in the euro area
affiliations: European Central Bank (ECB) and European Central Bank (ECB)

detail.title: Current account and monetary policy in the euro area
detail.abstract: We investigate how domestic and external shocks shape current account and monetary policydynamics in the euro area, a question of particular relevance for countries operating under a commoncurrency. We estimate an open-economy structural vector autoregression (VAR) with zero andsign restrictions derived from a multi-country DSGE model to identify economically meaningfulshocks. Examining Germany, Italy, and Spain, we find that domestic investment and preferenceshocks drive the current account and interest rates in opposite directions, whereas external demandand productivity shocks move both variables in the same direction. We also document spilloversfrom US preference shocks and US monetary policy shocks to euro area macroeconomic conditions.Using a counterfactual analysis that shuts down the interest rate channel, we show that monetarypolicy has only a limited influence on current account adjustment: while the absence of interestrate responses amplifies output and inflation volatility, the response of the current account remainslargely unchanged across shocks. Overall, our results highlight that, under a common monetary policy,current account dynamics in the euro area are primarily driven by macroeconomic shocks ratherthan by short-term interest rate movements.

title: Peaceful Agreements to Share a River
affiliations: Ashoka University and Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, School of Business and Economics

detail.title: Peaceful Agreements to Share a River
detail.abstract: This paper develops a model of conflict resolution over scarce water in a trans-boundary river. In our model,  we consider countries that are located along a river  and made a military investment.  Given these investments and their location along the river, they sequentially bargain over the surplus of water, or decide to engage in a military conflict with their upstream neighbour.  The probability of winning a military conflict is determined by a contest success function which depends on the military investments made before. We speak about a peaceful agreement if the countries rationally decide to bargain over the water instead of engaging into a military conflict. We show that,  if all benefit functions are nonnegative, increasing and concave, then for every  level of military investment, there always exists a peaceful agreement where every country prefers to bargain peacefully for the water. We provide a scenario that yields one such a peaceful agreement.

title: Capturing Temporal Anchor-Viewer Dynamics for Sales Prediction in Live Streaming E-Commerce: A Multimodal Deep Learning Approach

detail.title: Capturing Temporal Anchor-Viewer Dynamics for Sales Prediction in Live Streaming E-Commerce: A Multimodal Deep Learning Approach
detail.abstract: Real-time interaction between anchors and viewers is a unique and critical component of live streaming e-commerce, fostering relational bonds and driving immediate purchasing decisions. However, existing sales prediction models predominantly rely on aggregated behavioral metrics, overlooking the temporal and bidirectional nature of interactions that fundamentally shape sales outcomes. Our descriptive analyses of 7,684 broadcasts reveal that sales performance is driven by distinctive temporal trajectories of engagement, not merely aggregated levels. To address these limitations, we propose AVITSNet (Anchor–Viewer Interaction-aware Time Series Network), a multimodal deep learning framework that explicitly models the temporal and reciprocal dynamics of live streaming interactions. Experimental evaluation demonstrates that AVITSNet significantly outperforms conventional and hybrid baselines across all metrics. Ablation studies confirm that textual signals—capturing anchor speech and viewer comments that constitute the core of interaction—contribute most critically to prediction, while numerical behavioral and contextual features provide essential complementary value. Moreover, attention analysis reveals that the model assigns high attention to early viewer responses, indicating the predictive importance of initial engagement. By modeling how temporal trajectories and bidirectional interactions unfold over time, this study offers an interpretable and actionable approach to understanding and predicting sales performance in live streaming e-commerce.

title: Analyzing Aesthetics from the Perspective of the Holy Quran and its Crystallization in Organizational Communication

detail.title: Analyzing Aesthetics from the Perspective of the Holy Quran and its Crystallization in Organizational Communication
detail.abstract: Topic: The study of aesthetics provides the possibility of better understanding of phenomena and changing people's views. This article explains beauty from the perspective of the Holy Quran and its crystallization in the field of organizational communication. Method: In the current research, by analyzing the theme and using reliable sources, selected verses, and searching for the word aesthetics and its derivatives, the model of Barwan and Clark has been considered. Findings: By identifying verses related to beauty, and analyzing and investigating them, its managerial implications were presented in the field of organizational communication. Conclusion: analysis and deliberation in the verses of the Quran can provide a deeper religious look at organizational nature, internal and external communication, work ethics, and organizational values. The Qur'an mentions important ethics that can provide the basis for ethical organizational communication. This includes respecting the rights of employees, fairness in management, and creating a healthy work environment. Aesthetics based on Quran helps researchers and managers to analyze organizational concepts from different angles. This approach helps to develop our understanding of the role of religious principles in the organizational environment and to create an organizational environment that fits religious values.

title: Reducing Workplace Incidents / Poor Performance by Holding Organisations and Leaders Accountable by

detail.title: Reducing Workplace Incidents / Poor Performance by Holding Organisations and Leaders Accountable by
detail.abstract:
This study investigates the intricate link between workplace operational incidents and administrative errors, emphasizing the critical role of organizational and leadership accountability in mitigating error-enforcing conditions that precipitate incidents and degrade performance. Employing a robust qualitative approach, the research integrates a mixed-methods design encompassing naturalistic observation—both participant and non-participant—and unstructured interviews conducted with over 300 personnel within a Nigerian-based transnational organization. Data were meticulously analyzed using descriptive and deductive reasoning frameworks to elucidate the impact of leadership decisions and organizational practices on the prevalence of workplace errors and related incidents.

The findings reveal a compelling pattern: more than 80% of workplace incidents, encompassing both physical injuries and psychological harm, originate from administrative errors linked to leadership styles and organizational culture. Key error-enforcing conditions identified include pervasive blame culture, inadequate fatigue management, favoritism, bullying, flawed performance appraisal systems, and a pronounced lack of employee empowerment. Notably, psychological injuries arising from these administrative errors—such as diminished self-esteem, depression, and chronic stress—were found to be more detrimental than physical injuries, exerting profound negative effects on employee motivation, productivity, and overall organisational performance. The study further underscores the frequent misinterpretation of incident causality and highlights the paramount importance of objective evaluation and leadership accountability as mechanisms to reduce incident recurrence effectively.

In conclusion, the research advocates cultivating accountability at all organisational levels, enhancing leadership competencies, and promoting a culture grounded in empathy and objectivity within performance appraisal and incident management processes. Implementation of these measures is projected to foster safer, more productive work environments, thereby driving improved organisational outcomes. The study also calls for integrating accountability principles into corporate governance frameworks. It emphasises the need for transformational learning through causal reasoning to address the root causes of workplace errors and incidents, ultimately contributing to sustainable organisational excellence.

title: High-Praximity Economics: Reducing Transaction Cost Latency in Distributed Supply Chains via Digital Praxis Interfaces

detail.title: High-Praximity Economics: Reducing Transaction Cost Latency in Distributed Supply Chains via Digital Praxis Interfaces
detail.abstract: The transition to Energy Sovereignty in post-agrarian economies is currently inhibited by a "Praxial Gap": the temporal latency between capital availability (Global North) and infrastructure deployment (Global South). Drawing on the Dynamic Capabilities framework of Teece (2007) and the Ecosystem Strategy of Adner (2017), previous research (FitzGerald, 2025) established the "Vine Theory" of development, identifying the "Hub-and-Spoke" aggregation of neglected biomass as the structural pathway to energy independence. However, the financial orchestration of thousands of micro-suppliers remains prohibitively expensive under contemporary financing models. This paper proposes a new theoretical framework, Praxis Theory, to resolve this "First Mile" capital inefficiency. Synthesizing Williamson (1979) work on Transaction Cost Economics (TCE) with Ostrom, Tiebout & Warren (1961) principles of Polycentric Governance, we introduce Praximity as a universal standardised metric for supply chain efficiency. We formally define Praximity as the inverse function of temporal latency and coordinator friction between a peripheral actor's intent and a verified physical impact. While empirically grounded in the energy sector, this framework possesses universal validity for any distributed value chain characterised by Akerlof (1970) information asymmetry, from ethical retail provenance to disaster relief logistics. We argue that traditional finance suffers from "Low Praximity" due to high agency costs. In contrast, a Digital Praxis Interface, utilising Grieves (2024) Intelligent Digital Twin architecture allows "Peripheral Actors" to engage in "Asset Sponsorship," instantly funding physical tools for specific harvesters. This mechanism decouples asset financing from debt schedules, effectively closing the Praxial Gap. Using comparative statics analysis, this study demonstrates that increasing the Praximity Score (𝑃) accelerates the "Speed to Originality," allowing decentralised networks to build infrastructure faster than centralised state actors.

title: Valorising Municipal Solid Waste for Energy Sovereignty: A Techno-Economic Analysis of Logistical Constraints in Post-Agrarian Economies

detail.title: Valorising Municipal Solid Waste for Energy Sovereignty: A Techno-Economic Analysis of Logistical Constraints in Post-Agrarian Economies
detail.abstract: Rapidly digitising post-agrarian economies face a "Speed-Originality" paradox: the ambition to leapfrog into Industry 4.0 is frequently undermined by a "kill-switch" vulnerability-chronic reliance on imported cross-border energy. This paper argues that digital sovereignty cannot exist without energy sovereignty. By integrating Vine Theory with the Theory of Constraints (TOC), this study reclassifies Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) from a sanitation liability to a strategic "Soil" for national infrastructure. Utilising secondary data from the Asian Development Bank and techno-economic viability thresholds established by (Toba et al., 2024, p. 174) The analysis isolates the logistical bottlenecks preventing Waste-to-Energy (WtE) adoption in Cambodia. The findings reveal a stark dichotomy: while the capital (Phnom Penh) faces a collection efficiency constraint, secondary economic zones (Siem Reap) face a critical volume constraint, where seasonal waste generation frequently drops below the 500 Tonnes Per Day (TPD) thermodynamic efficiency floor. To resolve this deficit, we propose a Hub-and-Spoke logistics model that treats agricultural residue (rice straw) as a "spoke" to stabilise baseload capacity. This study concludes that WtE is fundamentally a supply chain challenge rather than a technological one, providing a blueprint for developing nations to achieve the energy independence necessary for digital innovation.

title: Public Standard Contract as Benchmark and Informed Opt-Out

detail.title: Public Standard Contract as Benchmark and Informed Opt-Out
detail.abstract: This article proposes a market design mechanism for standard contracts in relationhips between firms and consumers, based on the preparation, by a public authority, of a sectoral standard contract intended to serve as a benchmark. The standard is constructed in such a way as to maximize the expected surplus for the majority of consumers, eliminating or reducing contractual opacity, unexpected clauses, and litigation costs. Companies remain completely free to deviate from the public model, but the deviation must be signaled through a highly salient and standardized notice, which makes the consumer immediately aware of the departure from the recommended standard. In the event of deviation, it is up to the consumer to choose whether to enter into a contract that deviates from the model prepared by the public authority or to turn to a different firm. The article is part of the economic analysis debate on default rules, altering rules, and the failure of informed consent in mass markets, proposing a different approach to the problem, focused on the design of information signals rather than on procedural restrictions on opt-out. Taking a critical approach to the theories of Ayres, Ayres and Schwartz, and Gillette, it argues that an informationally salient opt-out can reduce decision-making errors without increasing procedural costs, preserve contractual innovation, and improve dynamic efficiency. The efficiency analysis identifies the conditions under which the model is often preferable to the main regulatory alternatives and discusses its possible failure modes, showing how the proposed approach offers a convincing response to the structural problems of consumer contracts.

detail.abstract: We use theory from identity economics, which synthesizes research characterizing how personal identity shapes decisions in domains such as education and career selection, to predict that the process by which people sort into accounting careers produces a population of accountants with a distinctive set of values. Specifically, we hypothesize that two kinds of personal values, called conservation values and self-enhancement values, are overrepresented among accountants because they are associated with the decision to work as an accountant. Using data from 38 countries in the European Social Survey, we find support for both hypotheses. Given this evidence that accountants’ values prioritize stability over change and concern for self over concern for others, we further hypothesize that, motivated by these values, accountants will be relatively skeptical about contemporary targets of social reforms, including those pursued by prominent accounting organizations. We test this prediction using attitudes about climate change and tolerance for minorities and find support for it. Based on our findings, we derive recommendations for an effective design of social reforms in the accounting profession. Our findings are relevant for accounting elites tasked with leading the profession into a dynamic future and contribute to the new and growing literature on accounting’s human capital.

title: Migration Policy Backlash, Identity and Integration of Second-Generation Migrants in France
affiliations: ,  and IÉSEG School of Management, Lille Campus

detail.title: Migration Policy Backlash, Identity and Integration of Second-Generation Migrants in France
detail.abstract: Do symbolic aspects of integration policies affect migrants’ integration into the host society? In this paper, we study the effects of a symbolic change in birthright citizenship rules in France that requires second-generation immigrants to state their allegiance on their integration. Adopting a Difference-in-Differences approach, we show that, contrary to its stated aim of fostering a greater sense of belonging, this policy led to a loss of national identity and an increase in perceptions of discrimination among the target group. We document that these effects are not driven by changes in naturalization rates or an increased general hostility. We also show that while the reform did not affect their economic or political integration, it did reduce their cultural integration, as measured by religiosity and naming patterns. Overall, rather than promoting integration, such migration policies can lead to a backlash.

title: Theory of Change in Creative Economy Policy Making: Stakeholder Engagement, Partnerships, and Trust – A Systematic Literature Review

detail.title: Theory of Change in Creative Economy Policy Making: Stakeholder Engagement, Partnerships, and Trust – A Systematic Literature Review
detail.abstract: Creative economy policy development increasingly relies on stakeholder engagement, creative partnerships, and industry trust as fundamental mechanisms for fostering innovation and supporting creative enterprises, yet emerging evidence reveals these collaborative mechanisms can systematically impede rather than facilitate effective policy outcomes under certain conditions. This systematic literature review employed PRISMA-ScR guidelines to analyze 120 studies from the Scopus database (2015-2024) examining how traditionally facilitating elements become constraining factors in creative economy governance, using Theory of Change frameworks to identify transformation patterns and paradoxical dynamics. The analysis reveals that stakeholder engagement evolves into consultation fatigue and artistic compromise, creative partnerships generate coordination overload and accountability dilution, and industry trust produces lock-in effects that stifle innovation through predictable transformation pathways involving threshold effects, power asymmetries, and institutional inertia. Traditional Theory of Change frameworks prove fundamentally inadequate for capturing these paradoxical dynamics, with only 28% incorporating negative pathways or unintended consequences, reflecting systematic optimistic bias that overlooks how collaborative mechanisms systematically transform from facilitators into constraints. The study proposes a Paradox-Aware Theory of Change framework that acknowledges multiple concurrent pathways, incorporates threshold effects where facilitating mechanisms transform into impediments, and recognizes contextual factors influencing transformation processes, enabling policymakers to anticipate and manage the dual nature of collaborative mechanisms rather than assuming universal benefits and supporting more adaptive creative economy governance strategies.

title: Startup Dynamics in Indonesia: Leveraging Lean Startup and Dynamic Capabilities for Growth and Sustainability

detail.title: Startup Dynamics in Indonesia: Leveraging Lean Startup and Dynamic Capabilities for Growth and Sustainability
detail.abstract: This study examines the development trajectory of digital startups in Indonesia by integrating Dynamic Capabilities Theory and the Lean Startup methodology. Employing a qualitative case study approach, we conducted semi-structured interviews with twelve senior executives and ecosystem enablers across fintech and healthtech sectors to explore how early-stage ventures navigate critical developmental phases. The research identifies six distinct stages of startup development—ideation, pre-seed, seed, launch and growth, maturity, and exit strategy—each characterized by unique challenges and strategic imperatives. Our findings reveal that successful startups leverage dynamic capabilities through iterative learning, rapid MVP experimentation, and continuous market feedback adaptation to achieve product-market fit despite resource constraints and regulatory uncertainties. The study highlights the instrumental role of Indonesia's startup ecosystem, particularly incubators, accelerators, and government initiatives, in providing critical resources and mentorship that enhance survival rates. However, significant challenges persist, including uneven geographic distribution of support services, suboptimal incubator effectiveness, and regulatory ambiguities. The research demonstrates that integrating dynamic capabilities with Lean Startup practices enables startups in emerging economies to overcome institutional challenges by enhancing sensing, seizing, and transforming capabilities. These findings offer valuable insights for policymakers designing supportive frameworks and practitioners seeking sustainable growth strategies in Indonesia's rapidly evolving digital economy.

title: Data-Driven Consumer Behavior Analysis for Strengthening Sustainable Halal Cosmetics Markets

detail.title: Data-Driven Consumer Behavior Analysis for Strengthening Sustainable Halal Cosmetics Markets
detail.abstract: The halal cosmetics industry in Indonesia continues to grow rapidly, driven by rising ethical consumption, sustainability awareness, and demand for product safety. However, the effectiveness of traditional demographic segmentation declines in mature markets with high levels of halal literacy. This study aims to assess whether demographic factors continue to influence the intention and purchasing behavior of halal cosmetics, or whether value-based variables have become more relevant. Using a quantitative cross-sectional survey design of 300 urban consumers of halal cosmetics, the data were analyzed using binary logistic regression, and all constructs were found to be reliable (α > 0.70). The results show that neither the intention nor the purchasing behavior model reached statistical significance, although income and occupation had the highest odds ratio values. The very high classification accuracy (>95%) indicates a ceiling effect, driven by the majority of respondents’ high intention and routine purchasing behavior. These findings confirm the limitations of demographic segmentation and the importance of data-based, psychographic, and value-based approaches in developing market strategies. The implications of this study are helpful to policymakers, marketers, and industry stakeholders in strengthening the development of a sustainable halal cosmetics market through more personalized, value-oriented strategies.

title: Is AI a Change Agent? How and Why

detail.title: Is AI a Change Agent? How and Why
detail.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has moved from a support technology to a core structural enabler of economic, social, and institutional transformation. Across the world, AI is reshaping productivity, value chains, and governance models. Global estimates suggest that AI could add around US$15–18 trillion to global GDP by 2030. More importantly, AI is redefining how decisions are made, how human cognition is augmented, and how institutions operate.

title: Sustainable Entrepreneurship Development Strategy for Achieving SDGs: A Conceptual Framework for SMEs

detail.title: Sustainable Entrepreneurship Development Strategy for Achieving SDGs: A Conceptual Framework for SMEs
detail.abstract: This research presents a conceptual framework, the Sustainable Entrepreneurship Development Strategy (SEDS), which encompasses six strategies for developing sustainable entrepreneurship in SMEs. The strategies include dynamic capabilities, innovative capabilities, stakeholder-focused approach, environmentally responsible practices, strong local ties, and excellent human resources. By implementing these strategies, SMEs can not only achieve long-term success but also contribute to addressing environmental and social challenges and fostering a more sustainable and inclusive economy. Although this study has limitations in terms of database selection and a lack of empirical evidence, it provides a foundation for future research to explore broader areas and validate the SEDS framework in real-world business settings, particularly in developing countries.

title: The Influence of Environment, Social, Governance and Leverage towards Profitability on the NYSE-Listed Energy Companies in the year 2024

detail.title: The Influence of Environment, Social, Governance and Leverage towards Profitability on the NYSE-Listed Energy Companies in the year 2024
detail.abstract: This study investigates the influence of Environmental, Social, Governance (ESG) factors and Leverage on the profitability of NYSE-listed energy companies in 2024. Using the Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) approach, the research aims to evaluate how sustainability practices and financial structure affect corporate performance during the global energy transition. The findings reveal that both the environmental and leverage dimensions have a significant and negative impact on profitability, indicating that high environmental compliance costs and elevated debt levels constrain short-term financial performance. In contrast, the social and governance factors exhibit no significant relationship with profitability, suggesting that their benefits may be more long-term and reputational rather than immediate. The results imply that while ESG integration is essential for maintaining legitimacy and investor confidence, it may initially reduce financial performance within energy firms undergoing structural and regulatory adjustments. These outcomes contribute to the growing debate on the short-term profitability trade-offs associated with sustainability adoption. The study underscores the importance of strategic financial planning and effective capital management to sustain profitability while advancing environmental and social objectives in the energy sector.

title: Reframing Transfer Pricing through Sustainable FAR: An Indonesian Context of Linking Sustainability Reporting, Performance, and Tax Risk Governance

detail.title: Reframing Transfer Pricing through Sustainable FAR: An Indonesian Context of Linking Sustainability Reporting, Performance, and Tax Risk Governance
detail.abstract: Transfer Pricing (TP) remains central to global taxation due to its implications for profit shifting, transparency, and accountability. The classical Functions–Assets–Risks (FAR) framework focuses mainly on financial and operational factors, overlooking sustainability dimensions that increasingly shape corporate value creation and fiscal legitimacy. This study conceptualises and advances the Sustainable FAR Framework—an extension of TP governance that embeds sustainability reporting, sustainability performance, and green accounting within tax-risk management. Using a qualitative, exploratory design, the research integrates practitioner-informed scoping with a PRISMA-guided Integrative Literature Review (2018–2024) that covers academic, regulatory, and corporate sources. Forty-two eligible studies were thematically synthesised, producing three pillars of Sustainable FAR: (i) sustainability reporting as evidence of economic substance, (ii) sustainability performance as a measurable indicator of economic contribution, and (iii) green accounting as a mechanism for environmental cost internalisation and fiscal incentives. The findings reveal that integrating ESG data into TP documentation enhances audit credibility, strengthens stakeholder trust, and aligns fiscal governance with Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) principles. Anchored in legitimacy and stakeholder theories, the framework redefines tax governance as an adaptive accountability process linking fiscal transparency with sustainable development. The study contributes theoretically by bridging transfer pricing, sustainability accounting, and governance theory, and practically by offering regulators, tax authorities, and corporations a model for embedding ESG accountability into fiscal policy and documentation.

title: The Cognitive Economy and AI

detail.title: The Cognitive Economy and AI
detail.abstract: This paper argues that the next major economic revolution will centre on human cognition rather than on physical or digital labour. As artificial intelligence progresses, it will increasingly monetise not just task-based labour but the latent intellectual, intuitive, and creative faculties of human minds. The next economic revolution will be defined not by the production of physical goods or the execution of routine digital tasks but by the monetisation of human cognition in its fullest complexity. In an AI-first world, human thought, intuition, creativity, and non-linear reasoning are emerging as the primary engines of value creation. As artificial intelligence progresses, it will increasingly monetise not just task-based labour but the latent intellectual, intuitive, and creative faculties of human minds. This paper introduces the concept of a cognitive economy in which human cognition, creativity, intuition, and neurodiversity become central economic assets, reshaping labour markets, organisational structures, educational paradigms, and societal institutions. Unlike prior technological shifts that primarily replaced manual or routine cognitive labour, AI amplifies and extends the human mind, enabling insights, ideas, and pattern recognition that were previously inaccessible to scale and translate into actionable, monetisable contributions. Within this framework, the cognitive economy operates through three interdependent mechanisms that collectively establish a new logic of human capital. First, augmentation occurs as AI systems extend and enhance human thinking, transforming intuition, creative insight, and spontaneous ideas into structured output that carries measurable economic value. Second, allocation arises through the development of cognitive marketplaces and platforms that match individuals with tasks, projects, and organisational roles aligned with their unique cognitive profiles, ensuring that divergent thinking and non-linear reasoning achieve maximal productive impact. Third, valuation evolves to reward originality, ideational influence, and non-linear reasoning rather than conventional metrics of hours worked, routine skills, or formal credentials. Together, these mechanisms create a system in which cognitive distinctiveness, adaptability, and creativity are recognised as core drivers of economic value, positioning human thought as an asset of unprecedented significance in the emerging AI-driven economy. The implications of this transformation are profound and far-reaching. Economically, traditional measures of human capital will be insufficient as value increasingly accrues to individuals capable of flexible thinking, complex pattern recognition, and imaginative problem solving. Socially, the cognitive economy offers the potential for recognition and inclusion of neurodivergent individuals whose cognitive profiles are naturally suited to innovation, while simultaneously posing the risk of novel forms of inequality and exploitation. Educational systems must pivot to cultivate cognitive flexibility, intuition, and creativity rather than focusing solely on information transmission or procedural knowledge. Policy frameworks will need to address questions of intellectual property, labour rights, AI governance, and fair compensation for cognitive contributions, ensuring that the monetisation of thought enhances rather than diminishes human agency and social equity. This paper integrates insights from human capital theory, cognitive science, artificial intelligence research, and neurodiversity studies to construct a cohesive theoretical model of the cognitive economy. It identifies critical challenges, including the measurement and assessment of non-linear skills, the equitable distribution of AI augmentation, and the ethical governance of cognition as a tradable resource. It also proposes a research agenda for empirical investigation, institutional experimentation, and policy innovation. By framing cognition as the central locus of economic value, this paper lays the intellectual foundation for a future in which human thought, intuition, and creativity are recognised, nurtured, and monetised on an unprecedented scale, providing a roadmap for understanding and shaping an AI-augmented economic paradigm that prioritises human intellectual potential.

title: Why Workers Binge-Watch: Insights from the Theory of Planned Behavior and Social Exchange Theory

detail.title: Why Workers Binge-Watch: Insights from the Theory of Planned Behavior and Social Exchange Theory
detail.abstract: Binge watching has become a widespread habit in the digital age, significantly impacting various aspects of life, including work productivity and social interactions. Vast evidence suggests significant implications to binge watching, including lower productivity, and worse mental health and overall wellbeing. This study aims to analyze binge watching behavior among workers using the Planned Behavior Theory and Social Exchange Theory as the conceptual framework. The research adopts a quantitative approach, utilizing Google Sheets and SmartPLS for data analysis. The sample, selected using  a snowball sampling technique, consists of 100 respondents who are of productive age, residing in Jabodetabek (Jakarta, Bogor, Depok, Tangerang, Bekasi) Indonesia Area, and engaged in employment or business activities. The analysis revealed that attitude and perceived behavioral control significantly influence the intention to binge-watch, while subjective norms show a weaker association. Intention strongly predicts actual binge-watching behavior among workers, supporting the applicability of the Theory of Planned Behavior in this context. Reward-cost evaluation, derived from Social Exchange Theory, demonstrates a direct positive effect on binge-watching behavior but not on intention. These results illustrate how cognitive and motivational factors collectively shape binge-watching habits within the working population. Future studies are encouraged to expand this model across diverse occupational and cultural contexts and to explore the long-term impacts of binge-watching on work-life balance and mental health.

title: Republic Act No. 9003: Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000

detail.title: Republic Act No. 9003: Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000
detail.abstract: This critique paper examines Republic Act No. 9003, known as the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000, which establishes a comprehensive framework for managing solid waste in the Philippines. The analysis highlights the law’s major components, including waste segregation, community-based programs, the establishment of Materials Recovery Facilities, and the prohibition of open dumpsites. While RA 9003 presents a well-structured and forward-looking approach, its effectiveness is hindered by weak enforcement, inconsistent implementation among Local Government Units, and limited public compliance. Despite these challenges, the law remains a significant step toward environmental sustainability. Strengthening institutional support, enhancing monitoring, and promoting continuous environmental education are essential for maximizing the law’s long-term impact.

title: Analyzing the Significance of Islamic Marketing in Enhancing Halal Cosmetics Purchase Intention of Indonesian Muslim Gen Z

detail.title: Analyzing the Significance of Islamic Marketing in Enhancing Halal Cosmetics Purchase Intention of Indonesian Muslim Gen Z
detail.abstract: As the countries with the largest Muslim populations, Indonesia and Malaysia can become the center of the world’s largest halal industry. From a study conducted by the researchers in 2024, which compared the intention to buy halal cosmetics of Indonesian and Malaysian Muslim Gen Zs, it was found that the intention to purchase halal cosmetics, with the moderation of each country’s government regulations to use them, was stronger in Malaysian Muslim Gen Z than Indonesian Muslim Gen Z. So this raises the question of whether there are other efforts that the Indonesian government can make to encourage this. Can Islamic Marketing, with its dimensions of Normative, Islamic Ethics and Social Welfare, in the forms of an Environmental sustainability approach and a Humanistic approach, achieve Indonesia’s goal of becoming a global hub for halal cosmetics? The purpose of this research is to analyze the significance of Islamic Marketing in increasing the intention of Indonesian Muslim Gen Z to purchase halal cosmetics, thereby realizing Indonesia’s commitment in this regard. The unit of analysis in this study is 250 Indonesian Muslim Gen Z individuals residing in the Jabodetabek area of Indonesia, aged 18-28 years, who are also cosmetics users, with Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) as the statistical tool. The findings of this study indicate that the influence of Islamic marketing on the intention of Indonesian Muslim Gen Z to purchase halal cosmetics is significantly positive. The social welfare dimension is the strongest influencer of the intention. This intention is further reinforced by the government’s obligation to use such products. The moderating effect of government regulations on their purchase intention outweighs the direct influence of each dimension of Islamic marketing on the intention to purchase. Large halal cosmetics business players in Indonesia can collaborate with the government to make optimal efforts to realize the government’s commitment.

title: Mapping the Cybersecurity Governance Research in Indonesia 2020-2025: A Qualitative Analysis

detail.title: Mapping the Cybersecurity Governance Research in Indonesia 2020-2025: A Qualitative Analysis
detail.abstract: This study aims to map the development of cybersecurity research in Indonesia. The scope of the study is limited to the years 2020-2025. This paper will employ a qualitative analysis to provide a clear visualization of these developments. The study will analyze 200 scientific journal articles by using machine learning to help retrieve a large amount of data from Google Scholar. The use of 200 articles as a sample size refers to the sample's adequacy and the principle of accuracy. This research found that cybersecurity research in Indonesia is connected to topics such as e-government, digital transformation, governance, personal data protection, and cybersecurity within the legal framework. The study recommends that future cybersecurity governance research focus on filling gaps in the existing governance framework.

title: Risk Management From A Behavioral Finance Perspective

detail.title: Risk Management From A Behavioral Finance Perspective
detail.abstract: According to classical finance theories, investors are expected to act rationally and manage risks based on objective data and mathematical models. However, behavioral finance challenges this assumption by emphasizing that individuals make financial decisions under cognitive limitations and psychological biases. This study explores the interaction between risk management and investor psychology within the framework of behavioral finance. It particularly focuses on key behavioral factors such as herding behavior, overconfidence, and loss aversion. Herding behavior can drive investors to mimic others, resulting in market bubbles or sudden crashes. Overconfidence leads individuals to underestimate risks and engage in excessive trading, while loss aversion explains why investors are more sensitive to potential losses than to equivalent gains. The methodology involves a conceptual review of the behavioral finance literature and its implications for risk management. The findings highlight that effective risk management requires more than quantitative models it must incorporate behavioral awareness and psychological insights to address the real drivers of investor behavior. The study concludes that integrating behavioral aspects into risk management frameworks can enhance decision quality, improve market stability, and support sustainable investment behavior.

title: Developmental State Theory and AI Governance: A Comparative Analysis of Innovation-Protection Balance in Singapore and Malaysia

detail.title: Developmental State Theory and AI Governance: A Comparative Analysis of Innovation-Protection Balance in Singapore and Malaysia
detail.abstract:
The rapid global deployment of Artificial Intelligence (AI) presents a fundamental governance challenge of balancing innovation promotion with regulatory protection. This study employs Developmental State Theory (DST) to explain divergent AI governance strategies in Singapore and Malaysia, two Southeast Asian nations with distinct economic development profiles but shared developmental state legacies.

We hypothesize that historical state capacity for strategic industrial policy, shaped by development stage, directly determines contemporary AI governance orientation. Our methodology combines qualitative comparative analysis of national AI policy frameworks with quantitative assessment of economic development indicators and AI exposure metrics.
Results reveal systematic differences reflecting the development stage. Singapore (GDP per capita $90,674.10), ranking 2nd globally in AI readiness, adopts highly permissive governance emphasizing "maximal space for innovation" through voluntary frameworks. Malaysia (GDP per capita $11,867.30, AI readiness rank 24th) pursues more cautious implementation, with policy constrained by acknowledged resource and expertise limitations. Both nations prioritize technological adoption over immediate legal stringency, but Singapore demonstrates significantly higher risk tolerance commensurate with its advanced economic capacity.

This pattern validates DST's core insight: state strategy varies systematically with the development stage. Just as developmental states historically calibrated industrial policy to their position in the global economic hierarchy, contemporary AI governance reflects similar logic. The study extends DST into the digital economy, demonstrating its continued explanatory power for understanding how states navigate technological transformation. Findings have implications for predicting governance evolution as middle-income nations advance economically and for understanding policy divergence within the broader category of developmental states.

title: Digital Transformation and Sustainability of MSMEs: A Systematic Literature Review

detail.title: Digital Transformation and Sustainability of MSMEs: A Systematic Literature Review
detail.abstract: In the era of Industry 4.0, digital transformation has emerged as a key element driving the competitiveness of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) while also aligning with the pursuit of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Although a growing body of literature has addressed this theme, there remains a scarcity of integrated reviews that combine findings from diverse research streams. This study responds to that gap by conducting a systematic literature review aimed at exploring research trends, identifying gaps, and showcasing the contributions of prior studies on how digital transformation supports MSME sustainability. Using the PRISMA framework, the review involved the identification, screening, and thematic assessment of works published between 2013 and 2023 in Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar. Seventy-eight studies were included for further analysis. The outcomes provide both theoretical mapping of research directions and practical guidance for policymakers, industry actors, and academics in developing sustainable and inclusive digital transformation strategies for MSMEs.

title: Republic Act No. 9003: Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000

detail.title: Republic Act No. 9003: Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000
detail.abstract: Republic Act No. 9003, or the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000, is one of the most significant environmental laws in the Philippines. It seeks to establish a comprehensive and systematic solid waste management program, focusing on waste reduction, segregation, recycling, and proper disposal. Despite its strong legal framework, challenges remain in its implementation across local communities. This critique discusses the core provisions of the law, its strengths, weaknesses, and overall impact.

title: Jakarta Smart City: Realizing Effectiveness & Efficiency of Electric Public Vehicles

detail.title: Jakarta Smart City: Realizing Effectiveness & Efficiency of Electric Public Vehicles
detail.abstract: This article aims to analyze Jakarta as a global city by evaluating the effectiveness and efficiency of electric public vehicles to realize the Jakarta Smart City. This study seeks to examine the multifaceted challenges, encompassing issues within government bureaucracy as well as those arising from public engagement and societal dynamics. This article finds that electric public vehicles are widely perceived as effective, especially due to their favourable impacts on environmental sustainability, public health, passenger comfort, and the enhancement of the city's image. The DKI Jakarta government has attempted to integrate the implementation of the SDGs within the framework of Smart City development through a program for the use of electric public transportation. Survey data indicate that the effectiveness of electric public transportation as part of the Jakarta Smart City implementation effort focuses on aspects of safety, comfort, and public trust.

title: Effect of Foreign Direct Investment on Capital Market Development in the MINT Economies: A Reflection of Complementarity or Substitutability Hypothesis?
affiliations: Modibbo Adama University of Technology - Department of Banking and Finance

detail.title: Effect of Foreign Direct Investment on Capital Market Development in the MINT Economies: A Reflection of Complementarity or Substitutability Hypothesis?
detail.abstract: The four countries, Mexico, Indonesia, Nigeria, and Turkey, popularly called the MINT economies, have been regarded as another group of developing countries that have advantageous positions, geographically, economically, and demographically, to influence global growth substantially. These countries have attracted foreign direct investment (FDI), which is expected to affect their financial markets, including the capital market. However, the effect could be positive (complementarity hypothesis) or negative (substitutability hypothesis). Since the health of an economy is often gauged by its capital market, this study, therefore, while testing the hypotheses, investigated the effect of foreign direct investment on capital market development in the MINT economies, during the period 1993-2023. The quantitative data used in the study, obtained from the World Development Indicators, were analysed using the Panel Autoregressive Distributed Lag (P-ARDL) technique. The study found a long-run, positive, and significant impact of FDI on capital market development. However, in the short run, FDI was found to exert a negative and significant impact on capital market development in the MINTs. Specifically, in the short run, FDI had a negative, non-significant impact on capital market development in Mexico, Turkey, and Indonesia, but an adverse, significant effect in Nigeria. The study concludes that FDI inflows promote capital market development in the MINT economies. It is therefore recommended that governments implement policies, principles, strategies, and programmes to stimulate inflows of foreign direct investment into the MINT countries. Also, some shock absorbers should be put in place in the MINTs, particularly in Nigeria, to cushion the short-run, negative impact of FDI on capital market development.

detail.abstract:
Central Bank Digital Currencies (CBDCs) have attracted significant global interest in recent years in parallel to developments in the broader payments landscape that have led to a considerable increase in digital payments, including technological innovation, introduction of new digital assets, expansion of private digital payment methods, and world events like the COVID-19 pandemic. Several countries have now been exploring CBDC as a potentially new form of central bank money in digital form to co-exist with and complement current forms of money.

Although legal architecture is a critical component of CBDC, the legal aspects of CBDC are significantly underexplored in academic literature. The purpose of this article is to address some of the key legal issues arising from retail CBDCs. The article first gives an overview of the main features of CBDCs and current global trends and then addresses some emerging legal questions along with suggestions for further consideration and awareness in this area. It does so by focusing on legal status and classification of retail CBDCs, privacy and data protection issues, public-private interaction in the CBDC ecosystem, and cross-border implications of CBDCs.

title: Multiple Voices, Intersecting Identities, and Relational Landscapes: A Narrative Inquiry into Migrant Women's Career Development
affiliations: Griffith University, Griffith University - School of Psychology, University of Queensland and Griffith University

detail.title: Multiple Voices, Intersecting Identities, and Relational Landscapes: A Narrative Inquiry into Migrant Women's Career Development
detail.abstract: Migrant women from economically developing countries who enter Australia while accompanying their husbands, face a great range of complexities that affect their career development. Grounded in the systems theory framework and an ethic of care, this research utilised narrative inquiry, through an exploratory multiple case study design, to explore the voices that shape the life-career narratives of former secondary-visa holder migrant women (SVMW) from economically developing countries. Six participants were recruited through purposive sampling for a semi-structured interview. Through a 'voice-centred relational method of analysis,' the operations of several influential, unique, and contrapuntal voices were noted. The findings challenge individualistic notions of agency, highlighting relational agency and the value of research that centres care and voice to amplify SVMW's oftenoverlooked experiences, thereby promoting social justice. This research contributes to theory, research, practice, and policy by amplifying SVMW's voices and highlighting the need for culturally responsive approaches to their career development.

title:
Carbon-Aware AI for ESG Investing & Eco-Gen AI

A Review of Carbon Aware Generative AI Technologies for ESG Investing
affiliations: University College London and University College London

detail.title:
Carbon-Aware AI for ESG Investing & Eco-Gen AI

A Review of Carbon Aware Generative AI Technologies for ESG Investing
detail.abstract: This paper reviews research in Carbon-Aware computing and introduces a new concept titled “Eco Gen AI” (EGAI). CarbonAware computing aims to reduce the environmental impact of computing by adopting less carbon-intensive energy sources and methods across high consumption technologies, such as server farms, data centres, Large Language Model (LLM) training, and blockchain proof-of-work systems. Eco-Gen AI defines an endto-end novel framework that leverages LLMs to develop environmentally aware portfolios through optimised LLM prompt engineering. EGAI exists in the intersection of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) investing, focusing on the emerging field of sustainable machine learning in Generative AI (Gen AI). Many ESG investment strategies have a mandate to positively contribute to the social and/or environmental wellbeing of shareholders, clients, and society. However, investors often fail to recognise their own ‘carbon footprint’ caused by the implementation of costly AI models, such as Gen AI and LLMs, which require substantial compute from ever-growing server farms. Together with the escalating size of datasets required to train LLMs, AI models have contributed to a significant increase in global data centre expenditure, rising from $250.5 billion in 2016 to $325.9 billion in 2023, with the latest projections suggesting $6.7 trillion might be required by 2030 [1].

title: Climate Disclosure and the Transformation of Gatekeeping

detail.title: Climate Disclosure and the Transformation of Gatekeeping

publicationDetails.detailsText: European Corporate Governance Institute - Law Working Paper No. 887/2025
Washington University in St Louis Legal Studies Research Paper Forthcoming

detail.abstract:
How might enhanced climate disclosures disrupt the verification practices of gatekeepers in capital markets transactions? This essay explores this question, using the SEC’s now-stayed 2024 Climate Rule as a guide.

The essay begins by examining the established architecture of gatekeepers’ verification practices. These are complex, yet standardized, relying on a web of experts, each with their own area of specialization, constructed in response to liability concerns. Enhanced climate disclosures are likely to expand the responsibilities of traditional gatekeepers, especially securities underwriters, while also prompting issuers to rely on attestation providers—green gatekeepers who certify the accuracy and completeness of registrants’ greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions metrics and other climate information. The essay considers how these verification practices must change to sustain due diligence defenses under federal securities law, as verification increasingly requires environmental expertise.

The essay concludes by addressing a core policy question: Should GHG emissions metrics be certified by experts? While expert certification can improve accuracy, the essay argues against such expertisation, in contrast to the approach in the Climate Rule. The Securities Act ensures that liability for these disclosures must fall somewhere: if not with experts, then with underwriters. Even if underwriters now lack the environmental expertise of attestation providers, they have unique incentives and capabilities to shift risk to the right gatekeepers, to monitor those gatekeepers effectively, and they have a track record of doing so.

title: Digital Startup Dynamics: Ambiguity, Transition, Funding, and Sustainability Strategies

detail.title: Digital Startup Dynamics: Ambiguity, Transition, Funding, and Sustainability Strategies
detail.abstract: This research provides a comprehensive understanding of the startup development landscape in Indonesia, shedding light on the distinct stages, critical success factors, and key challenges that startups must navigate to achieve sustainable growth and success. The findings highlight the pivotal role of the early stages - ideation, pre-seed, and seed - in laying the foundation for a startup's long-term prospects, while also underscoring the significant risks characterizing these foundational phases. As startups transition into the launch and growth stage, the emphasis shifts toward market execution, scalability, and attracting investor interest, with successful navigation propelling them toward further funding rounds and potential exits. The post-scale advancement stage marks a significant transition, where startups evolve into established technology companies, with a focus on achieving profitability and global expansion, and strategic considerations such as IPOs, acquisitions, or remaining as profitable private entities. The research also emphasizes the pivotal role of the startup ecosystem, with the government, incubators, accelerators, and collaborative efforts among stakeholders playing crucial roles in nurturing and supporting the growth of entrepreneurial ventures. By providing a comprehensive understanding of the startup development process in Indonesia, this research offers valuable insights for policymakers, ecosystem stakeholders, and entrepreneurs themselves, informing the design of more effective policies, the enhancement of ecosystem support mechanisms, and the strategic decision-making of startup founders as they navigate the complex and dynamic landscape of the digital economy. While the study acknowledges its limitations, such as the focus on the Indonesian context and the reliance on qualitative data, it identifies opportunities for future research, including comparative studies across different regions, exploration of industry-specific dynamics, and investigation of the impact of digital technologies and ecosystem collaboration on startup success, all of which can contribute to a more comprehensive understanding of the factors driving startup success and the optimal strategies for fostering a thriving entrepreneurial ecosystem in the rapidly evolving digital economy.

title: Dynamic Compensation Optimization to Incentivize Spontaneous Engagement of Occasional Drivers in Last-Mile Delivery
affiliations: , University of the Bundeswehr Munich and University of Duisburg-Essen

detail.title: Dynamic Compensation Optimization to Incentivize Spontaneous Engagement of Occasional Drivers in Last-Mile Delivery
detail.abstract: To keep pace with the continuously growing e-commerce, many traditional brick-and-mortar retailers have launched online stores and home delivery services. However, despite substantial progress in the scientific literature, the last-mile delivery remains costly, eroding profit margins and undermining the scalability of such online store operation. In this context, the concept of occasional drivers, whereby in-store customers may occasionally become drivers who deliver to online customers, recently gained attention. However, existing approaches assume that the retailer possesses detailed information on potential occasional drivers, in particular on their individual destinations after instore shopping, and that the retailers can assign them delivery tasks. In this work, we relax these key assumptions: First, we assume that the availability of potential occasional drivers and their destinations are uncertain for the retailer. Second, we assume that retailers cannot assign tasks directly but can only adjust compensations dynamically to incentivize in-store customers to spontaneously perform a delivery. These relaxed assumptions result in a novel practice-relevant problem for which existing operational control approaches are inapplicable. Based on a Markov decision process formulation of the stochastic dynamic optimization problem, we analyze the problem analytically and derive as well as prove structural properties of optimal compensation schemes. Based thereupon, we develop a scalable heuristic solution approach. In a comprehensive numerical study, we demonstrate that the policy resulting from our approach generates substantial cost savings of up to 19% compared to literature-based benchmark policies. Further, our work yields insights into the potential of engaging unknown in-store customers as occasional drivers, such as the existence of economy-of-scale effects and characteristics of favorable engagement strategies. Moreover, we generate insights into designing effective compensation policies, such as the benefits on location-and time-dependent policies.

title: Predicting SME Default Risk: Machine Learning, High-Frequency Data, and Sectoral Heterogeneity
affiliations: , Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye and Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye

detail.title: Predicting SME Default Risk: Machine Learning, High-Frequency Data, and Sectoral Heterogeneity

All views and opinions expressed in this paper are solely those of authors and do not necessarily reflect the views of any affiliated institutions or organisations.
