detail.abstract: We combine high-frequency firm-level data with machine learning and sector-specific modeling to improve short-term default prediction for SMEs. Using quarterly data for nearly 500,000 Turkish firms from 2019 to 2024, we compare linear and non-linear models across seven main sectors and twenty-two sub-sectors. The results yield three key insights. First, machine learning models outperform traditional linear approaches. XGBoost delivers the highest predictive accuracy across most sectors, while Random Forest performs best in agriculture, showing that optimal algorithm choice depends on industry characteristics. Second, SHAP-based variable importance analysis uncovers strong heterogeneity across sectors, as the relevance of financial and operational variables varies substantially, exposing the limits of uniform credit-risk models. Third, sub-sector models capture default dynamics more precisely than aggregate sector models, exhibiting lower variance and greater responsiveness to sector-specific vulnerabilities. These results demonstrate that non-linear machine learning models exploit high-frequency data patterns more effectively than linear statistical models, particularly when calibrated at granular sectoral levels. By integrating highfrequency data with a short-term default estimation horizon, our approach enables earlier detection of risk buildup and more responsive monitoring of financial fragility. The findings provide actionable insights for policymakers, financial institutions, and regulators seeking to enhance early-warning systems and strengthen macroprudential oversight in SME-dominated economies.

title: Effects of International Airline Alliances on Domestic–International Connecting Passengers in Japan

detail.title: Effects of International Airline Alliances on Domestic–International Connecting Passengers in Japan
detail.abstract: This paper estimates the effect of international airline alliances on the volume of passengers connecting from domestic to international flights. Using data on Japanese domestic air services, the analysis focuses on the initial wave of alliance expansion by Japan's major carriers between 1995 and 2005. The identification strategy conceptually follows the spirit of a triple-differences (difference-indifference in differences) approach: it compares changes in passenger volumes between airlines that expanded their alliance participation and those that did not, and further contrasts passengers connecting from domestic to international flights (type I) with those traveling solely on domestic flights (type D) on the same domestic segments. The results indicate that alliance expansion significantly increased the number of type I passengers.

title: Zero-Equity CEO Pay
affiliations: University of North Texas, College of Business Administration, Department of Finance, Insurance Real Estate and Law, University of Connecticut - Department of Finance and University of Connecticut

detail.title: Zero-Equity CEO Pay
detail.abstract: Contrary to standard agency theory, one in seven large U.S. public firms grants CEOs zeroequity pay (ZEP) annually; over half do so at least once. We comprehensively document this practice, showing it cannot be explained by founding-family status or CEO equity ownership/incentives but is more prevalent among younger, riskier, and smaller firms. Crucially, ZEPs are less likely under greater public and investor scrutiny. In ZEP years, CEOs receive lower total but higher cash pay with simpler performance metrics, while maintaining performance outcomes and pay-for-performance sensitivity. Our findings suggest that public attention, rather than solely economic efficiency, helps enforce pay norms.

title: The Specificity Problem: Why Reformed Epistemology Cannot Justify Particular Religious Traditions

detail.title: The Specificity Problem: Why Reformed Epistemology Cannot Justify Particular Religious Traditions
detail.abstract: This paper examines a critical limitation in Alvin Plantinga's Reformed Epistemology: while it may successfully defend generic theistic belief against evidentialist critiques, it fails to justify belief in any particular religious tradition with its specific doctrines and truth claims. Reformed Epistemology argues that belief in God can be "properly basic"—rational without inferential justification—through the operation of the sensus divinitatis, a cognitive faculty that produces theistic beliefs under appropriate circumstances. However, I argue that this mechanism cannot bridge the gap between minimal theism ("something divine exists") and the detailed doctrinal content of Christianity, Islam, Hinduism, or any specific tradition. The sensus divinitatis delivers only generic awareness of transcendence, while particular traditions require acceptance of complex theological propositions about Trinity, prophethood, salvation, scripture, and metaphysics. This "specificity problem" is compounded by three factors: (1) contradictory specific beliefs across traditions cannot all be properly basic, (2) the strong correlation between birthplace and religious belief suggests cultural conditioning rather than basic cognitive response, and (3) appeals to revelation or scripture reintroduce the evidential requirements Reformed Epistemology sought to avoid. I conclude that particular religious traditions lack adequate epistemological justification through properly basic beliefs, leaving intellectually honest inquirers without grounds for choosing one tradition's specific claims over another's.

title: Centralization of Government and Legal Traditions in Hungary

detail.title: Centralization of Government and Legal Traditions in Hungary
detail.abstract: In the era of globalization, illiberal tendencies in nation states (including Hungary and other Central and Eastern European countries) face new challenges, such as the 2008 global economic crisis and international migration. After World War II in Western Europe and in the 1990's in Central and Eastern European countries, the dominant trends in public administration reforms were related to decentralization and privatization (in line with New Public Management theories). Public administration tasks and powers were transferred to local governments and non-governmental organizations. Autonomous institutions were also created in the executive branch. Contrary to these processes, the second decade of this century has seen serious centralization in Hungary and other Central and Eastern European countries (e.g. Poland). Local governments have lost a significant part of their powers and their fiscal autonomy in Hungary. The role of the Prime Minister and his apparatus has grown significantly, and the organization of the executive branch has become much more concentrated than before, for example, the number and role of ministries and certain central institutions has decreased. The main objective of this article is to determine which legal traditions have influenced these changes, namely, whether the so-called illiberal state can be defined within the framework of any existing legal traditions in Hungary. The main research methods of the paper are the analysis of relevant theoretical literature, policy documents, and legal norms.

title: An Integrated Framework of Agile Leadership, Trust, and AI Implementation: Impacts on Organizational Capabilities and Performance

detail.title: An Integrated Framework of Agile Leadership, Trust, and AI Implementation: Impacts on Organizational Capabilities and Performance
detail.abstract: The contemporary business environment demands effective artificial intelligence (AI) implementation strategies to achieve competitive advantages, yet organizations face significant challenges in translating AI investments into tangible outcomes. This study develops and empirically tests an integrated framework examining the relationships among management commitment, agile leadership factors, trust in AI, AI implementation, and organizational performance outcomes. Using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with data from organizations implementing AI technologies, the research reveals counterintuitive findings that challenge conventional assumptions. While management commitment strongly predicts trust in AI, trust does not significantly influence AI implementation success. Among agile leadership dimensions, only concrete organizational capabilities, specifically agile work environment and team skills, significantly drive implementation, while general agile leadership shows non-significant effects. AI implementation demonstrates powerful cascading effects on company competitiveness, knowledge management capacity, and dynamic capabilities, which subsequently enhance sustainable employee work performance. These findings suggest that AI implementation success depends more on tangible organizational capabilities than on psychological factors or leadership styles. The study provides evidence-based guidance for organizations, recommending prioritization of concrete capability-building initiatives over trust-building or general leadership approaches. This research contributes to theory by challenging trust-centric AI adoption models and extends agile leadership theory by distinguishing between general traits and specific capabilities, while offering practical insights for organizations navigating AI adoption in an increasingly AI-driven business landscape.

title: Designing Collaborative Contests under Feasibility Uncertainty
affiliations: Vanderbilt University - Owen Graduate School of Management, University of Dayton and University of California, San Diego (UCSD) - Rady School of Management

detail.title: Designing Collaborative Contests under Feasibility Uncertainty
detail.abstract: Many solution-seeking organizations are exploring the notion of open innovation to harness the creativity, diverse experience, and distributed problem-solving capabilities of external solver communities. Within this paradigm, reward-based innovation contests have emerged as a possible mechanism, helping to source ideas in relatively modular and lower-complexity domains such as logo design, product naming, and T-shirt graphics. However, these contest formats often struggle to scale to development-intensive or scientifically complex problems, where solvers face high uncertainty, resource constraints, or feasibility doubts that dampen sustained engagement. To address these limitations, we propose a more collaborative open innovation approach, in which seekers actively support solvers during the innovation process-by providing resources, infrastructure, data, or technical guidance to enhance solver effort. Importantly, we show that such collaborative contests can also address solver uncertainty regarding the problem feasibility and help in maintaining their engagement throughout the more demanding stages of solution development.

title: Fraud Hexagon Analysis in Detecting Potential Fraud in Financial Reports

detail.title: Fraud Hexagon Analysis in Detecting Potential Fraud in Financial Reports

keywords: changes in the board of directors

detail.abstract: This study aims to analyze the tendency of financial statement fraud using the fraud hexagon framework, which consists of stimulus, opportunity, rationalization, capability, arrogance, and collusion. These six elements are measured by the following proxies: financial targets, frequency of audit committee meetings, auditor changes, changes in the board of directors, number of CEO photographs, and political connections. The population of this study includes infrastructure companies listed on the Main Board and Development Board of the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) as of December 31, 2024. The research sample was selected using a purposive sampling method, resulting in a total of 87 observations over a three-year observation period from 2022 to 2024. The data used were obtained from audited financial statements and annual reports published on the IDX. Data analysis was conducted using logistic regression models. The findings of this study suggest that political connections exert a positive and significant influence on the likelihood of financial statement fraud. In contrast, financial targets, the frequency of audit committee meetings, auditor changes, changes in the board of directors, and the number of CEO photographs do not affect the likelihood of financial statement fraud.

title: Accounting Information System Analysis on Credit Sales to Improve The Effectiveness of Internal Control at PT. Jeje Harapan Transindo

detail.title: Accounting Information System Analysis on Credit Sales to Improve The Effectiveness of Internal Control at PT. Jeje Harapan Transindo
detail.abstract: The purpose of this research is to analyse the credit sales accounting information system and internal control at PT Jeje Harapan Transindo. This research is a case study. Data were obtained through interviews, questionnaires, and documentation. The data analysis technique used was descriptive analysis of the sales accounting and internal control systems, drawing conclusions from the analysis, and providing recommendations. Based on the analysis, it can be concluded that the credit sales accounting and internal control systems at PT Jeje Harapan Transindo are still not functioning as intended. Payment discrepancies frequently occur due to ineffective internal controls, such as the late collection department failing to collect from customers approaching their payment deadlines, resulting in customers paying past the agreed-upon deadline. The sales department also does not monitor the credit history of prospective customers before accepting new orders, and no credit limits have been established for each customer. In its implementation, the company must provide clear Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) regarding the separation of responsibilities between the collection and sales departments to ensure the proper management of accounts receivable.

title: The Role of the DBFOM Scheme in Strengthening Public-Private Partnerships for Village-Owned Enterprises (BUMDes) Development: Opportunities, Risks, and Socio-Economic Impacts in Mina Jaya Lamongan

detail.title: The Role of the DBFOM Scheme in Strengthening Public-Private Partnerships for Village-Owned Enterprises (BUMDes) Development: Opportunities, Risks, and Socio-Economic Impacts in Mina Jaya Lamongan
detail.abstract: This paper examines the implementation of the DBFOM (Design-Build-Finance-Operate-Maintain) model within the framework of Public-Private Partnerships (PPP) for the development of Village-Owned Enterprises (BUMDes) in Indonesia. The DBFOM model, which encompasses the full project life cycle-from design and construction to financing, operation, and maintenance-has emerged as an effective strategy to bridge funding gaps and address inefficiencies in public sector projects. This study utilizes a systematic literature review of fifteen peer-reviewed journal articles published between 2020 and 2025, focusing on the interplay between government policy, private investment mechanisms, and community-based enterprise development. The findings reveal that DBFOM contributes to enhancing BUMDes performance by improving efficiency, expanding financing sources, and distributing risks more equitably between the public and private sectors. Nonetheless, the study identifies persistent challenges, including unequal power dynamics, limited local governance capacity, and inadequate risk management frameworks. Furthermore, the paper argues that the successful application of DBFOM requires transparent contractual arrangements, local capacity strengthening, and participatory monitoring mechanisms. By integrating governance, financial, and community development perspectives, this paper enriches the understanding of hybrid financing models in advancing sustainable rural economies. It also underscores the importance of adaptive policy interventions to reinforce local ownership and accountability in PPP-based rural development initiatives. The recommendations offered aim to provide valuable insights for policymakers, practitioners, and researchers engaged in rural economic revitalization and partnership-based development models.

title: Digital Technology Capabilities and Firm Performance: A Meta-Analytic Review

detail.title: Digital Technology Capabilities and Firm Performance: A Meta-Analytic Review

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interest

detail.abstract: Digital capabilities have become paramount for sustaining a competitive advantage, driven by the accelerated proliferation of digital technologies and their transformative impact on how firms create value. However, research on digital capabilities is fragmented and lacks a systematic framework that integrates diverse forms of digital capabilities and their combined impact on firm performance, resulting in inconsistent findings. Following a psychometric meta-analysis and random-effects model procedures, this meta-analytic review synthesizes evidence from 145 empirical studies, comprising 162 effect sizes and 198,026 firm-level observations. Results reveal that digital capabilities have a moderate yet overall positive impact on firm performance (r = 0.45). Notably, the influence on financial performance (r = 0.49) is greater than on non-financial performance (r =0.440). Examining specific archetypes, I found that digital business capabilities have the largest effect on performance, followed by digital innovation capabilities and digital platform capabilities. Additionally, digital sensing and digital analytics capabilities also demonstrate significant positive impacts. Furthermore, moderator analysis indicates that contextual factors such as industry type, business type, firm size, and economic development considerably influence these relationships. My findings provide nuanced insights into the multifaceted role of digital capabilities, informing managers on how to enhance firm performance through strategic digital investments.

title: Why Consumers Feel Closer to Brands that Overshare: An Academic Analysis of Transparency, Vulnerability, and Digital Intimacy

detail.abstract: Brand communication has undergone a major shift in the social media era, with many companies adopting a more open and personal tone in their interactions with consumers. This includes the sharing of behind-the-scenes details, founder emotions, early failures and day-today processes. This practice, commonly referred to as "brand oversharing," has become increasingly common among modern direct-to-consumer brands. This research paper examines why oversharing fosters consumer closeness, focusing on psychological factors such as vulnerability, parasocial intimacy, relatability and transparency. The paper relies on secondary research, including consumer trust studies, social media reports, and selected brand case examples. Findings suggest that oversharing functions as an authenticity mechanism, reduces skepticism, and encourages emotional bonding. The paper concludes with implications for marketers, limitations and suggestions for future research.

title: Digital Transformation and AI Integration in Lebanese Higher Education: An Explanatory Sequential Mixed-Methods Study
affiliations: Sultan Qaboos University - College of Nursing and Lebanese University

detail.title: Digital Transformation and AI Integration in Lebanese Higher Education: An Explanatory Sequential Mixed-Methods Study
detail.abstract: This study examines the interplay between digital transformation initiatives, artificial intelligence (AI) integration, and student satisfaction in Lebanese higher education. An explanatory sequential mixed-methods approach was employed, with data collected from 300 undergraduates at three Lebanese University campuses. Quantitative findings revealed significant dissatisfaction with current digital systems (78%), together with substantial optimism concerning AI's potential for personalized learning (85%). Regression analyses identified infrastructure quality (β = .42, p < .001), system reliability (β = .38, p < .001), and technical support (β = .31, p = .002) as significant predictors of satisfaction, accounting for 58% of the variance. Qualitative content analysis identified four main barriers: interface usability, functionality gaps, system integration challenges, and inadequate technical support. These results highlight the importance of human-centered, contextually appropriate digital transformation that prioritizes robust infrastructure, integrated systems, and sustainable AI implementation.

title: The Perfect Storm of Transnational Enforcement: Litigation Funding, Foreign Forums and Severe Substantive Law in the Mariana v BHP Case

detail.title: The Perfect Storm of Transnational Enforcement: Litigation Funding, Foreign Forums and Severe Substantive Law in the Mariana v BHP Case
detail.abstract: The collapse of the Fundão tailings dam in Mariana, Brazil, in 2015 has generated one of the most complex transnational disputes in contemporary environmental law. In November 2025, the High Court in London found BHP liable under Brazilian environmental law and the Brazilian Civil Code in a mass claim brought on behalf of hundreds of thousands of Brazilian claimants. At the same time, litigation funders, specialised claimant firms and a sophisticated English procedural framework for group litigation transformed the case into a global legal and financial event. This article argues that the Mariana v BHP litigation is not merely another chapter in the story of cross-border mass torts. It is a paradigmatic instance of what may be called a "perfect storm of transnational enforcement": a convergence of (i) powerful third-party litigation funding, (ii) a foreign forum institutionally equipped to handle mass claims, and (iii) a particularly severe body of substantive law travelling extraterritorially. In Mariana v BHP, capital, jurisdiction and Brazilian environmental norms combined in a way that dramatically magnified corporate exposure. The paper proposes a simple analytical triangle of transnational risk-funding, forum and law-and situates the Mariana litigation at its centre. It discusses the role of third-party funders in turning otherwise impossible claims into financially viable projects; the emergence of the English courts as a hub for ESG-related mass torts; and the significance of Brazilian strict and integral risk liability being applied by a foreign court to a UKlinked multinational. The article concludes by exploring the implications of this "perfect storm" for corporate governance, risk management and legal policy in both home and host states.

title: The Linguistic Collapse Of "Brand": Semantic Inflation And Definitional Failure In Marketing Discourse

detail.title: The Linguistic Collapse Of "Brand": Semantic Inflation And Definitional Failure In Marketing Discourse
detail.abstract: The term "brand" has become ubiquitous in business discourse, yet exhibits fundamental definitional incoherence. This study examines whether "brand" has undergone semantic inflation to the point of operational uselessness, preventing systematic implementation, academic teaching, and measurable outcomes. The research employed a three-part analysis: (1) etymological tracing from Old Norse brandr through contemporary usage, (2) cross-linguistic comparison across English, Spanish, French, and Mandarin to determine universality of semantic expansion, and (3) substitution testing to assess whether "brand" retains unique definitional content distinct from synonyms like "business," "reputation," or "identity." The analysis reveals systematic definitional collapse across all three dimensions. The term evolved from concrete physical marker (burned mark on livestock) to abstract concept encompassing contradictory meanings (logo, reputation, promise, feeling, story, experience, culture). Cross-linguistic analysis shows parallel semantic inflation in marca, marque, and 品牌 (pǐnpái). Substitution tests demonstrate that "brand" can be replaced with multiple unrelated terms without semantic loss, indicating definitional emptiness rather than precision. This collapse has produced decades of misalignment between academic theory, industry practice, and public understanding, preventing the term from functioning as a coherent analytical unit. By documenting this breakdown, the paper clarifies why "brand" can no longer be treated as a stable construct and argues for renewed conceptual precision in both scholarly and commercial use. This analysis provides a foundation for future research to develop more precise, operationalizable terminology capable of replacing the current ambiguity.

title: Technological adoption and Firm Resilience: Understanding the Impact of New Digital Technologies
affiliations: National Institute of Statistics (Istat), University of Bari, Government of the Italian Republic (Italy) - National Institute of Statistics (ISTAT), Scuola Superiore Sant'Anna and Scuola Superiore Sant'Anna di Pisa - Institute of Economics

detail.title: Technological adoption and Firm Resilience: Understanding the Impact of New Digital Technologies
detail.abstract: This study investigates the impact of new digital technologies on the resilience of firms to external shocks. Using rare comprehensive data on both the adoption of single and multiple new digital technologies, we employ a Difference-in-Differences methodology with propensity score matching to evaluate how digitalization influenced firms’ ability to withstand the COVID-19 crisis. We isolate the effects of adopting 1) a single technology, 2) multiple technologies (the breadth of adoption), and 3) technologies that are complementary to one another. The findings provide novel insights into how firms can shape their investments in new digital technologies to increase the benefits of digitalization, and enhance their ability to navigate future crises.

title: Motivational Climate Effects on Communications, Emotional-Social States, and Performance in Collaborative Gaming Environment
affiliations: Reichman University, College of Management Academic Studies and Reichman University

detail.title: Motivational Climate Effects on Communications, Emotional-Social States, and Performance in Collaborative Gaming Environment
detail.abstract: The study explores the effects of motivational climate on communication patterns, emotional states, collective efficacy, and performance in collaborative gaming environments. Forty participants with no prior gaming experience were randomly assigned to 20 gender-matched teams of three (including one confederate) across two motivational climates: positive-supportive (PS) or neutral-unsupportive (NU) (10 teams per condition). Team members completed three progressively difficult levels of the video game Overcooked! 2 during which communication contents, emotional responses, collective efficacy, and performance outcomes were observed and coded. Results revealed that PS team members significantly outperformed NU teams at lower task difficulty level, but this advantage diminished as task complexity increased. Communication analysis revealed that PS team members used significantly more action-oriented, factual, and emotional statements, while NU team members used more statements of uncertainty and non-task-related communication. PS team members maintained more positive emotional profiles throughout, with higher excitement and happiness scores and lower anxiety, dejection, and anger compared to NU team members. While collective efficacy declined with task difficulty, this pattern was similar across both conditions. Surprisingly, performance differences disappeared at the highest difficulty level, revealing that when tasks become extremely complex, the advantages conferred by positive-supportive motivational climates may reach their limits, with task demands potentially overriding psychological benefits.

title: Multi-Stakeholder Marketing: Mapping the Field
affiliations: University of Turin, University of Turin - Department of Management,  and University of Turin

detail.title: Multi-Stakeholder Marketing: Mapping the Field
detail.abstract: Multi-stakeholder marketing is growing in importance, both in theory and practice. However, it still appears poorly conceptualized as an integrated discipline, and its applications are untapped. Therefore, this paper delves into such a concept by conducting a systematic literature review (SLR) to uncover how multi-stakeholder marketing has evolved, its applications for marketing and societal outcomes, and future research and practical directions. Our findings, overall, reveal a growing consensus among scholars on the importance of engaging diverse stakeholders in marketing value-creation processes, moving from narrow to interconnected relationships. We outline that most studies addressing multi-stakeholder marketing appear in the traditional marketing field rather than the corporate and/or social/green marketing segments. However, they are still dominated by an instrumental perspective that leverages multi-stakeholder engagement to serve pure marketing scopes, such as creating a competitive advantage and leaving social issues aside. While still residual, this represents an advancement in the field, and we argue that traditional marketing strategies should broaden their applications by engaging interconnected stakeholder groups that naturally open the traditional marketing boundaries to society. We provide our conceptualization of multi-stakeholder marketing, including key characteristics, based on observed best practices and arguments, which will serve as a basis to elaborate practically and theoretically in the future.

title: Virtual Influence and Material Aspirations: A Socio-digital Study of Hyper-consumerism in Kerala's Non-Urban Populace
affiliations: Government College Madappally, Kozhikode, Government College Madappally, Kozhikode, Government College Madappally, Kozhikode and Government College Madappally, Kozhikode

detail.title: Virtual Influence and Material Aspirations: A Socio-digital Study of Hyper-consumerism in Kerala's Non-Urban Populace
detail.abstract: The consumer lifestyle and consumption pattern in Kerala in recent years has been transformed significantly due to the rapid economic growth and increasing digital influence. In this backdrop, this paper examines the extent and the factors of hyper-consumerism in the non-urban population in the state of Kerala. A descriptive research design was used to collect data in the number of 116 respondents using a structured questionnaire. The results show that younger, educated, and digitally active people are predisposed to hyper consumption and largely due to virtual environments, such as online marketplaces, and social media. The paper points out that digital payment systems especially UPI have only increased the impulsive buying behaviour by bringing ease and immediacy in the buying process. The statistical tests prove the high levels of associations between the demographic variables, virtual engagements and the determinants of hyper-consumerism. All in all, the findings are indicative of both cultural and economic transition towards material aspiration whereby consumption is a sign of identity and modernity. The paper highlights the importance of digital literacy and responsible consumerism that would be able to guarantee sustainable consumption trends in non-urban Kerala.

title: Strategic Organizational Behavior and Managed Attrition: A Multi-Level Analysis of Intentional Employee Turnover at Motherson Sumi Systems

detail.title: Strategic Organizational Behavior and Managed Attrition: A Multi-Level Analysis of Intentional Employee Turnover at Motherson Sumi Systems
detail.abstract: This paper conducts a multi-level organizational behavior analysis of "managed attrition" at Motherson Sumi Systems (MSSL), focusing on cases where the organization implicitly or explicitly prefers employee exits. Using OB frameworks such as the Job Demands-Resources Model, Social Exchange Theory, Psychological Contract Theory, and Structural Signaling Theory, the study explains system-driven behavioral cues that nudge talent segments toward voluntary separation. The research integrates qualitative case patterns, organizational data designs, and theoretical constructs to explore how organizations use cultural levers, communication patterns, performance systems, and structural ambiguity to produce predictable attrition outcomes. The study concludes with ethical considerations and HR governance recommendations for organizations practicing managed attrition in emerging markets.

title: Analyzing Aesthetics from the Perspective of the Holy Quran and its Crystallization in Organizational Communication

detail.title: Analyzing Aesthetics from the Perspective of the Holy Quran and its Crystallization in Organizational Communication
detail.abstract: Topic: The study of aesthetics provides the possibility of better understanding of phenomena and changing people's views. This article explains beauty from the perspective of the Holy Quran and its crystallization in the field of organizational communication. Method: In the current research, by analyzing the theme and using reliable sources, selected verses, and searching for the word aesthetics and its derivatives, the model of Barwan and Clark has been considered. Findings: By identifying verses related to beauty, and analyzing and investigating them, its managerial implications were presented in the field of organizational communication. Conclusion: analysis and deliberation in the verses of the Quran can provide a deeper religious look at organizational nature, internal and external communication, work ethics, and organizational values. The Qur'an mentions important ethics that can provide the basis for ethical organizational communication. This includes respecting the rights of employees, fairness in management, and creating a healthy work environment. Aesthetics based on Quran helps researchers and managers to analyze organizational concepts from different angles. This approach helps to develop our understanding of the role of religious principles in the organizational environment and to create an organizational environment that fits religious values.

title: A Kingdom Divided, Partly Strong, Partly Brittle: An Analytical Observation of Institutional Decline in Modern Europe and the British Monarchy

detail.title: A Kingdom Divided, Partly Strong, Partly Brittle: An Analytical Observation of Institutional Decline in Modern Europe and the British Monarchy
detail.abstract: This paper considers the modern decline of institutional authority through the lens of Daniel 2:41-43. The passage describes a structure that stands upright yet lacks internal strength. It describes a kingdom that carries the appearance of unity but cannot hold together. This study argues that the present transformation of the British monarchy and the broader weakening of European institutions reflect this pattern in a concrete and observable way. This is not a speculative argument. This is an analytical description of how political, cultural, and religious systems behave when their legitimacy erodes quietly rather than through force. The paper situates this decline within the tradition of legal realism and institutional analysis, while also recognizing the theological dimension that has shaped Western thinking for centuries.

title: The Unicorn Problem: How Identity Worksheets Manufacture Confusion, Not Education

detail.title: The Unicorn Problem: How Identity Worksheets Manufacture Confusion, Not Education

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Part of the Bocchinfuso III Canon- a must read if you ask me.

detail.abstract: Between 2015 and 2025, K-12 classrooms saw an influx of identity-themed educational tools such as "The Gender Unicorn," "Genderbread Person," and "Identity Circles." These worksheets ask children to "place themselves" along abstract spectrums of gender identity, expression, attraction, and orientation-categories that require cognitive capacities children do not yet possess. This micro-paper argues that such materials constitute developmentally inappropriate identity priming, not education. They shift ideological burdens onto children, collapse pedagogical purpose into emotional sorting, and blur the boundaries between family, psychology, and public instruction. The result is not inclusion but confusion-a form of epistemic destabilization at the earliest ages.

title: Integrating Monthly Salary Investment with High-Standard Research Paper Production: A Comprehensive Strategic Framework

detail.title: Integrating Monthly Salary Investment with High-Standard Research Paper Production: A Comprehensive Strategic Framework
detail.abstract: Academic researchers face a persistent tension between financial security and intellectual productivity. This document presents an integrated framework demonstrating how systematic monthly salary investment strategies, when properly structured, actually enhance rather than detract from research output quality. Through evidence-based financial planning and time optimization techniques, physiotherapy researchers and other academics can achieve simultaneous goals: sustainable wealth accumulation, reduced financial stress, and maintained or improved research publication standards. The framework emphasizes automation, strategic task batching, cognitive protection, and delegation as mechanisms through which financial discipline supports rather than impedes academic excellence. By implementing a "financial infrastructure" requiring <5 minutes monthly attention, researchers protect their high-value cognitive capacity for manuscript development, data analysis, and intellectual contribution. This document integrates contemporary research on financial stress effects on academic performance, time management optimization for professionals, and evidence-based personal finance strategy to create a practically implementable system tailored to the Indian research context.

declarations.ethicsApproval: This research is based on secondary data, published literature, and industry practices. No human participants, patients, or personally identifiable data were involved. Therefore, no ethics approval or consent was required for this study.

detail.abstract:
This study examines how Critical Path Analysis (CPA), a project-management technique
used to plan and control complex processes, can be applied to marketing and
merchandising operations in the fashion sector. The research identifies how timing, task
dependency, and production delays affect product launch cycles, promotional calendars,
and supply-chain coordination. Through case analysis of fashion brands and
merchandising cycles, the study demonstrates that applying CPA reduces lead times,
improves communication between marketing and production teams, and enhances
overall profitability. The findings suggest that fashion businesses can optimize seasonal
planning, product delivery, and marketing campaigns using critical-path tools.

title: Effect Of Different Levels of Carrageenan PGP on the Yield of Selected Soybean Varieties

detail.abstract:
Soybean is one of the essential leguminous crops in the Philippines and is mainly utilized for food and feed production. However, the local production of soybean has been insufficient to cater to the demand for the crop. Thus, the Philippines still relies on imports from other countries. With this, the study aimed to determine the effect of the different levels of Carrageenan PGP on the yield when applied to selected soybean varieties. Specifically, it aimed to evaluate the adaptability of soybean genotypes to the frequency of Carrageenan PGP application. This study was conducted in Barangay La Paz, Magalang, Pampanga.

The study utilized four treatments, namely: T1 (Negative control); T2 (100 ppm PGP); T3 (150 ppm PGP); T4(Farmer’s Practice). Two varieties of soybean were considered as sub-treatment; V1 – PSB SY 2 and V2 – CL Soy 1. The experiments were laid out using a Two-factor factorial adopting the Randomized Complete Block Design (RCBD) with four replications. Data were analyzed using the Analysis of Variance, and differences were determined using the Least Significant Difference (LSD).

Application of Carrageenan PGP at 150 ppm to soybean significantly gave a positive effect on the following parameters: tallest plant height at maturity with a mean of 73.96 cm; produced the highest number of pods per plant of 72.08; provided the highest number of seeds per pod of 2.39; attained 15.13g and recorded as the heaviest weight of 100 seeds, obtained the highest yield of 1.78 to 2.02 mt/ha. Meanwhile, the highest shelling percentage was gained from both treated plants with PGP  at a rate of 100 and 150 ppm ranging from 56.66 to 58.91, respectively. 

 In addition, Carrageenan PGP at 150 ppm provided a net income of Php 28,450.00- 35,650.00/ha, with an ROI of 114.03%-142.89% regardless of the variety and an added benefit of 5.39-7.06 was obtained. However, there was no interaction among the types across all parameters.

title: Eurocentric Ethics and Pakhtunwali in Northwest Pakistan: Decolonising Qualitative Research

detail.title: Eurocentric Ethics and Pakhtunwali in Northwest Pakistan: Decolonising Qualitative Research
detail.abstract: Purpose-While conducting research in non-Western contexts, local cultural values confront conventional research ethics, which results in methodological difficulties. It is significant for researchers to know the problems and the ways they can manage them. Design/methodology/approach-Using a decolonial and autoethnographic approach, in this article, I reflect on issues encountered during two rounds of fieldwork on the Taliban's insurgency (2007-2009) in northwestern Pakistan. I focus on the data-collection phase. Findings-The major difficulties related to how local values of Pakhtunwali, such as hospitality, bravery, honour and gender differences, challenge research ethics such as confidentiality, informed consent, voluntary participation, equal representation and beneficence. I argue for integrated research approaches that adhere to Eurocentric ethics but are culturally appropriate in a non-Western context, facilitating researchers and positively impacting the researched community. Research limitations/implications-Researchers need to know how to respond to the difficulties. It is hoped that the insights of this article will contribute to good research practices among those who research indigenous communities, especially the Pakhtuns in northwest Pakistan. Originality/value-The decolonial efforts have become a rich body of discourse, but decolonising research in the context of Pakhtunwaali (the culture of Pakhtuns) in Pakistan requires greater attention. Methodological difficulties that occur due to applying the Eurocentric approach in the northwest region of Pakistan is a significant area to explore.

title: Is Australia Reliving Japan's Housing Bubble? An Econometric and Machine Learning Assessment

detail.title: Is Australia Reliving Japan's Housing Bubble? An Econometric and Machine Learning Assessment
detail.abstract: This paper investigates whether contemporary housing prices in Australia constitute a speculative bubble that echoes Japan's late 1980s real estate boom. Using annual and quarterly data from the early 1980s to 2025, we analyse national and citylevel house prices in Australia, compare them to Japan and to a set of global high-cost cities, and estimate the degree to which observed prices can be justied by macroeconomic and structural fundamentals. Methodologically, we combine (i) a dynamic panel fundamentals model (System GMM), (ii) city-specic cointegration and vector error-correction models (VECM), and (iii) a random forest model with Shapley decompositions calibrated on the crosscountry framework of Kohlscheen (2023). We construct an explicit misalignment index and a Japan Echo indicator that quantify deviations of Australian housing valuations from fundamentals and from the historical Japanese experience. Our results suggest that Australian prices are in a Fragile Equilibrium. While valuations are stretched, the structural drivers dier fundamentally from Japan's 1989 experience. Panel estimation reveals a signicant global credit elasticity (β = 0.43), but Australian price dynamics are heavily anchored by credit availability (77% explanatory power) rather than supply constraints (23%). Critically, our VECM estimation yields an adjustment parameter of α = −0.0169, implying an exceptionally weak mean-reversion mechanism. The paper concludes with policy implications regarding tax settings, macroprudential regulation, and the vulnerability to exogenous income shocks.

title: Meeting Household Energy Needs through Community Forestry: A Systematic Review of Evidence from Nepal
affiliations: Prince of Songkla University (PSU), Prince of Songkla University (PSU), Wisdom Academy and Research Centre and Wisdom Academy and Research Centre

detail.title: Meeting Household Energy Needs through Community Forestry: A Systematic Review of Evidence from Nepal
detail.abstract: The availability of clean and affordable household energy has been long-standing in rural Nepal, with household biomass sources taking over the household consumption. This paper examines the role of community forestry in providing households with energy security, promoting social inclusion, and sustaining the environment. The review uses a systematic approach guided by the PRISMA 2020 standards and synthesises the evidence from 92 empirical studies on the issue published since 2004. Web of Science, Scopus, and NepJOL were used to gather data based on inclusion criteria for community forestry, household access to energy, and participatory governance. The conceptual framework used to evaluate the interaction between human, natural, social, financial, and physical capitals and governance systems to determine household energy outcomes was the Sustainable Livelihoods Approach (SLA). Results indicate that community forests are the primary source of fuelwood and other forest products for 6090 percent of rural households, cut household energy costs by up to 18 percent, and enhance forest restoration in 85 percent of the studies examined. This improves transparency and meaningful representation, as well as forest conditions and biodiversity. Nevertheless, inequities include elite capture, the underrepresentation of women and marginalised groups, and poor uptake of cleaner technologies, which hinder equal gains. The findings highlight that community forestry contributes substantially to the welfare of rural communities. Still, sustainable energy transitions require reforming policies to set energy targets in forestry strategies, advance alternative energy technologies, and enhance intergovernmental coordination under federal governance. The study finds that incorporating household energy objectives into community forestry policies is essential for achieving the Nepal Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs 7, 13, and 15). It suggests an adaptive governance system, participatory governance, and technology-based interventions to fast-track the transition of the rural energy system toward cleaner, more equitable systems.

title: Consumption as the Foundation of the Economic System: Reclaiming the Market's Original Purpose to Serve Human Well-Being

detail.title: Consumption as the Foundation of the Economic System: Reclaiming the Market's Original Purpose to Serve Human Well-Being
detail.abstract: Prevailing economic models treat consumption as a derivative variablean outcome of production, capital allocation, or utility maximization. This paper argues that this view is fundamentally inverted. Consumption is not a component within the economic system; it is the system ' s foundation. The market exists because humans consume; production, capital formation, and firm behavior arise in response to this primordial fact. By repositioning consumption as the ontological basis of the economy, we reveal a profound misalignment in modern institutional design: the economic system frequently prioritizes profit extraction, structural optimization, or capital reproduction at the expense of the human beings it was originally created to serve. This paper reconstructs a human-centered economic paradigmone in which consumption reshapes markets, restores economic agency to individuals, and reorients economic systems toward the well-being of people rather than their sacrifice.

title: Cost Of Implementing A "Quality" Tourism Model

detail.title: Cost Of Implementing A "Quality" Tourism Model
detail.abstract: Since 2007, the island of Ibiza has experienced an extraordinary boom in five-star hotels with around twenty hotels newly open, most of them the result of local business initiatives. These openings mark a dramatic change of model, since most of Ibiza's hotels at the beginning of the twenty-first century were of medium or low category. While the overall supply of rooms has not increased in number, the new hotels require much more staff and consume a far greater volume of resources of all kinds. Moreover, the change in the tourism model has been sudden and unexpected, resulting in significant impacts on the island's economy and society, most seriously in the area of housing and labour relations.

title: The Crumbling of Francoist Spain's Isolationism Thanks to Foreign Currency Brought by European Tourists in the Early Years of the Golden Age

detail.title: The Crumbling of Francoist Spain's Isolationism Thanks to Foreign Currency Brought by European Tourists in the Early Years of the Golden Age
detail.abstract: The 'Golden Age' refers to an era of rapid economic growth which led to dramatic changes within European society. The steady rise in income coupled with recently introduced paid holidays encouraged the new middle classes to emulate the lifestyle of the glamorous and privileged trendsetters of the Belle Époque and the 1920s. The outward trappings of this included the purchase of a car and annual holidays in the Mediterranean, amounting in the 1950s to a sort of yearly pilgrimage. In the Balearic Islands and the Costa Brava an ample tourist sector flourished against a political background that was essentially in opposition to it-the autarchic stage of the Franco regime. Tourism, in the end, became one of the determining factors which provoked radical changes to this regime, leading eventually to complete abandonment of its militant isolationism.

title: A Survey of Natural-Language Driven Command-Line Assistants and Intelligent Shell Systems
affiliations: Pimpri Chinchwad University, , Pimpri Chinchwad University, Pimpri Chinchwad University, Pimpri Chinchwad University and Pimpri Chinchwad University

detail.title: A Survey of Natural-Language Driven Command-Line Assistants and Intelligent Shell Systems
detail.abstract: The command line interface has been a cornerstone of system administration, software development, and automation for decades, serving professionals and power users alike. However, its usability has always been constrained by cryptic syntax requirements, the burden of memorizing countless commands, and often unclear error messages. Recent breakthroughs in artificial intelligence especially large language models and natural language processing are now poised to revolutionize how we interact with traditional CLIs by introducing intelligent, conversational interfaces that can understand what users actually want to do, diagnose what went wrong, and generate working commands from plain English descriptions. This survey brings together the latest research and practical system developments in natural language powered command line assistants and automated shell systems. We start by looking at how CLIs have evolved historically and examining early automation technologies, tracing the journey from manually crafted scripts to neural network approaches that harness the capabilities of modern transformer models. The paper presents a systematic way to classify intelligent shell systems based on their underlying model architecture, how they decide whether to execute commands, their safety measures, and their strategies for handling errors. We evaluate several representative systems including ShellGPT, Warp AI, Copilot CLI, and our own hybrid assistant that combines both local and cloud-based language models using detailed comparison matrices and real world use case analysis. We dive deep into the major challenges these systems face: hallucinations where the AI generates incorrect commands, ambiguous error messages that are hard to interpret, limited training data, and serious security concerns. Finally, we explore where future research should head, imagining the next wave of autonomous system administration agents, secure on device AI inference, and voice controlled CLI automation. This survey contributes a unified classification system, an extensive literature review, empirically grounded comparisons between systems, and practical recommendations for researchers and developers who want to build robust, intelligent command line automation tools.

title: Bass Reeves and the Jurisprudence of Archival Insurgency: Corrective Remembrance as Jurisprudence in the Reconstruction of Suppressed History

detail.title: Bass Reeves and the Jurisprudence of Archival Insurgency: Corrective Remembrance as Jurisprudence in the Reconstruction of Suppressed History
detail.abstract: This paper develops a framework for understanding historical recovery as a form of jurisprudence. Through the life and erasure of U.S. Deputy Marshal Bass Reeves (1838–1910), it demonstrates how archival work can function as juridical correction rather than mere documentation. When Reeves's record—arguably one of the most extraordinary in nineteenth-century American law enforcement—was suppressed, a juridical wrong occurred: a violation of the right to truthful historical representation. The methodology advanced here, Corrective Remembrance as Jurisprudence, interprets archival recovery as a constitutional act of redress. This framework treats the restoration of erased histories as analogous to legal proceedings: gathering evidence, challenging precedent, and issuing rulings on truth. Drawing on Art T. Burton's path-breaking research, alongside scholars such as Alaina E. Roberts, Murray R. Wickett, Saidiya Hartman, Christina Sharpe, and Tina Campt, this paper treats memory as a site of constitutional accountability. The framework includes explicit discussion of methodological limitations in historical reconstruction and the challenges of working with systematically suppressed archives. Reeves's restoration to history exemplifies what I term archival insurgency—the collective labor through which silenced truths reclaim evidentiary sovereignty.

title: Regime-Based Portfolio Allocation Using Hidden Markov Models and Reinforcement Learning

detail.title: Regime-Based Portfolio Allocation Using Hidden Markov Models and Reinforcement Learning
detail.abstract: This study develops a regime-aware portfolio allocation framework that combines Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) with Reinforcement Learning (RL) to dynamically allocate across equities (SPY), long-term Treasuries (TLT), and gold (GLD). Using daily ETF data from 2004-2025, a three-state Gaussian HMM chosen via the Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) identifies low-volatility, transitional, and high-volatility regimes, consistent with recent findings on nonlinear market dynamics (Ardia et al., 2024; Gupta & Pierdzioch, 2023). We evaluate both rule-based and RL-driven allocation strategies in an out-of-sample setting. The RL policy achieves the strongest Sharpe ratio while preserving interpretability through regime-conditioned portfolio weights, illustrating how RL can enhance HMM-based regime identification in tactical asset allocation.

title: Aggregating Heterogeneous Supply and Demand: Micro-level Strategies and Emergent Macroeconomic Dynamics

detail.title: Aggregating Heterogeneous Supply and Demand: Micro-level Strategies and Emergent Macroeconomic Dynamics
detail.abstract: This paper develops a dynamic framework to reconstruct the law of supply and demand by explicitly modeling heterogeneous consumer demand and staircase-shaped aggregate supply curves. By aggregating individual consumer valuations and firm production decisions, the model captures how micro-level heterogeneity shapes dynamic market behavior, generating fluctuations in prices, quantities, and market structure over time. The framework produces multiple types of equilibrium-including optimal, interval, and jump equilibrium-which arise endogenously from the interaction of demand and supply heterogeneity, without relying on representative agents or exogenous shocks. We illustrate these mechanisms through a proof-of-concept simulation, showing how the interplay of heterogeneous preferences and discrete supply structure alone can produce rich and realistic patterns in aggregate market outcomes. This approach provides a unified, tractable framework for analyzing dynamic supply-demand interactions in heterogeneous markets and offers insights into the fundamental sources of macroeconomic fluctuations.

title: Green and Sustainable Technologies: Impact on the Environment. Exploring Sustainability in Agriculture Supported by Minimum Support Price (MSP): Sohna, Haryana, India Case Study
affiliations: KR Mangalam University, KR Mangalam University and KR Mangalam University

detail.title: Green and Sustainable Technologies: Impact on the Environment. Exploring Sustainability in Agriculture Supported by Minimum Support Price (MSP): Sohna, Haryana, India Case Study

keywords: Minimum Support Price Policy in India's State of Haryana
Crop Diversity Techniques Like Crop Rotations
Resource Optimization Strategies for Soil Health Improvement Through Precision Farming Methods

detail.abstract: Agriculture aiming for sustainability is now recognized as crucial for maintaining food supplies while minimizing ecological harm, especially where traditional farming practices predominate. In India's MSP program, which provides farmers with guaranteed minimum crop prices like rice and millet at set rates, it ensures their economic security through stable income levels for farming activities. Despite its role in bolstering economic stability, MSP is linked to extensive farming practices characterized by heavy reliance on synthetic fertilizers, herbicides, and substantial irrigation demands, resulting in detrimental effects such as land degradation, diminished freshwater supplies, and environmental disruptions that may go unnoticed initially. This study examines how incorporating eco-friendly agricultural techniques into MSP-supported farming operations within the Sohna area, Haryana, enhances environmental sustainability. The main goal of this study is to assess how green and eco-friendly agricultural techniques affect the ecological health of MSP-operated farms located within the Sohna district of Haryana State, India. This research involves analysing data qualitatively. Our main approach involved conducting indepth farmer surveys among 120 participants supported by MSP programs; this ensured our study's population reflected various socioeconomic backgrounds, farm sizes, and genders accurately. Comparisons between solar-powered irrigation systems, organically produced crops, biodegradable fertilizers, precise agricultural methods like precision farming, and traditional rotational planting revealed differences concerning ecological metrics such as freshwater usage, reliance on synthetic chemicals for fertilizer and pest control, soil quality improvement, and overall yield efficiency. Secondary data was retrieved through governmental documents related to MSP procurements, extension services for agriculture, as well as prior research into sustainable farming practices within semiarid areas. Various analytical techniques were employed; these encompassed descriptive statistical analyses alongside approaches for assessing technological uptake rates through logistic regressions aimed at identifying socioeconomic factors influencing tech acceptance, complemented by correlational studies designed to elucidate connections between technological utilization and ecological impacts. Studies show that when these agriculturalists adopted eco-friendly practices, they significantly reduced their reliance on resourceconsuming materials. The water consumption decreased significantly by about 30%, while both chemical fertilizers and pesticides were drastically cut down nearly 50% less than in traditional methods of agriculture. Significant enhancements were observed for soil quality metrics, resulting in markedly superior conditions of soil fertility and nutrient accessibility within Green Technology farming operations. It is crucially important to remember that crop yields remained consistent under conditions where sustainability did not affect production levels nor were they costly through participation in MSP programs. Logistic regression showed that factors such as land size, educational attainment, and family income significantly influence whether individuals adopt green practices, yet they do not affect gender differences. Studies demonstrate significant relationships where increased use of technologies correlates strongly with higher consumption of resources; these findings also show beneficial connections in terms of improved soil quality due to technological advancements. Correlation analysis underscores the ecological advantages associated with adopting such strategies sustainably. This study reveals that certain ecofriendly agricultural techniques might inadvertently compromise crop yields while aiming for greater ecological balance within MSP-driven farming systems. These outcomes hold significant importance for policy makers, agronomists, and outreach teams as they highlight crucial actions required to foster environmentally friendly methods; especially tailored towards subsistence farming communities. Integrating eco-technologies into management systems for peri-urban areas helps achieve sustainable ecology over time, mitigate adverse environmental impacts, and promote resilient agricultural practices specifically suited for arid zones like Sohna, India.

title: A Critical Analysis of Republic Act No. 9003: Evaluating Policy Strengths, Weaknesses, and Implementation Gaps

detail.title: A Critical Analysis of Republic Act No. 9003: Evaluating Policy Strengths, Weaknesses, and Implementation Gaps
detail.abstract: This paper critically examines Republic Act No. 9003, the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000, considering its policy framework, strengths, weaknesses, and practical implications for environmental regulation in the Philippines. Although RA 9003 presents a comprehensive and progressive view of solid waste management practices, focusing on source segregation, community involvement, and decentralization of responsibility to local government units, the practice reveals considerable gaps. These are limited resources between LGUs, the implementation of key provisions, and continued difficulties in the compliance of the population. The analysis underscores the impacts of these structural barriers on unequal implementation of the law and on the achievement of ecological goals of the law. The paper ends by giving recommendations on how to enhance institutional support, monitoring systems, public awareness, and multi-sectoral collaboration. In general, the critique highlights that, as a critical environmental policy, RA 9003 can only be effectively implemented in the long term with more coordinated, well-resourced, and community-based implementation plans.

title: The Relationship Between Financial Liability of Public Officer and Disciplinary Law

detail.title: The Relationship Between Financial Liability of Public Officer and Disciplinary Law
detail.abstract: This study aims to analyze the relationship between the financial liability of public officials and disciplinary law. Under the legal regulations and judicial decisions normative examination and analysis have been conducted in the study. It is argued that, within the framework of the principles of accountability, effectiveness, efficiency, and legality in public administration, the protection of public resources and the prevention of public damages are related to the functionality of financial liability and disciplinary law. The study reveals, in empirical terms, that financial and disciplinary obligations are based on different legal frameworks and procedures, yet they possess a functional unity in preventing public harm and protecting public resources. As a result, the study emphasizes the need to strengthen control mechanisms such as financial and disciplinary liability and to enhance the sense of responsibility among public officials.

title: From Civil Law to Precedent Governance? Brazil's Supreme Court, Health Litigation and the CNJ Practical Guide on Access to Medicines

detail.title: From Civil Law to Precedent Governance? Brazil's Supreme Court, Health Litigation and the CNJ Practical Guide on Access to Medicines
detail.abstract: Brazil has become an emblematic jurisdiction in the global study of health litigation. Over the last three decades, the interaction between a universal public health system (SUS), strong constitutional guarantees and uneven implementation of public policy has produced one of the largest bodies of health-related court decisions in the world. As litigation expanded, courts were repeatedly called to decide who should be sued, which level of government should pay for medicines, and what kind of evidence would justify overriding administrative choices. In 2019 and 2024, the Brazilian Supreme Federal Court (STF) attempted to systematize this phenomenon through two leading cases under its general repercussion docket-Theme 6 and Theme 1,234-and later consolidated their normative core in Binding Precedents 60 and 61. In 2025, the National Council of Justice (CNJ) issued the Practical Guide for Themes 6 and 1,234, a detailed institutional protocol that translates STF case law and interfederative agreements into operational flows on jurisdiction, funding and evidentiary thresholds for the judicial granting of medicines. This paper argues that the Guide is not merely an administrative tool, but a structural moment in Brazil's ongoing transition from a traditional civil law paradigm to a form of precedent governance that approximates some features of common law. By turning constitutional jurisprudence into standardized judicial behaviour-through binding precedents, intergovernmental agreements and CNJ soft-law instruments-Brazil is building a hybrid model of governance for social-rights litigation. The article situates the Guide within Brazil's constitutional architecture, examines its implications for access-tomedicines litigation, and suggests how this institutional experiment may inform comparative debates on judicialization, health governance and the design of precedent systems in civil law countries.

title: Caelinomics: The American Prosperity Plan

detail.title: Caelinomics: The American Prosperity Plan

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author has no relevant financial or non-financial interests to disclose. This work arose from independent research that began with personal analysis of public policy articles, identification of recurring patterns in legislative outcomes, and systematic review of publicly available U.S. Treasury, CBO, IRS, and BEA datasets. No external individual, organization, or entity suggested, directed, or influenced the research questions, methodology, or conclusions.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no funding from any source, public or private. It was conducted solely by the author in his personal capacity with the objective of developing and sharing a viable fiscal-reform framework that improves economic outcomes for all Americans.

detail.abstract:
Caelinomics is a comprehensive fiscal reform that replaces the current U.S. tax code with a single 10 % value-added tax (VAT) on non-essential consumption, eliminates broad tariffs, and redirects existing payroll contributions into personal retirement accounts. Key features include:

  • 10 % general VAT (0 % on essentials, graduated 10–30 % on luxury/dining)
  • Tariff consolidation into two targeted categories (20 % conflict-of-interest, 10 % supply/demand)
  • Elimination of taxes on tips and overtime
  • Full redirection of $1.8 T annual payroll taxes into individual 200K retirement accounts

The reform generates $6.9 T in annual federal revenue, produces a permanent $614B surplus beginning Year 1, and enables complete elimination of the national debt by 2048. Household purchasing power rises by $1,000 (middle-income) to $4,700 (lower-income) annually. Combined with universal basic healthcare and merit-based immigration reform, Caelinomics establishes a self-funding economic engine capable of sustaining American preeminence beyond 2100.

title: Broken Cities: Who's Behind Ghana's Urban Chaos?

detail.title: Broken Cities: Who's Behind Ghana's Urban Chaos?
detail.abstract: Ghana's cities continue to face persistent disorder despite decades of decentralization and reform. This study explores the structural and behavioral roots of urban dysfunction through a political economy and systems lens. It introduces the Multi-Actor Urban Disorder (MAUD) framework to model how fragmented authority, institutional overload, and civic noncompliance interact to produce chaos. Two additional tools, the Urban Governance Accountability Matrix (UGAM) and the Governance Load Index (GLI)-support the analysis by mapping accountability gaps and institutional stress. Simulation results show that partial or delayed reforms fail to reverse decay. Only early, coordinated, and high-intensity interventions that align mandates with capacity and build cross-actor accountability can stabilize the system. The findings offer a replicable model for diagnosing governance fragility and guiding reforms in rapidly urbanizing yet institutionally fragile sub-Saharan contexts.

title: The Universal Law of Adaptive Complexity: Formal Foundations and 31 Years of Empirical Validation

detail.title: The Universal Law of Adaptive Complexity: Formal Foundations and 31 Years of Empirical Validation
detail.abstract: I introduce and empirically validate the Universal Law of Adaptive Complexity, a fundamental principle governing when adaptive systems energetically justify their structural costs under environmental volatility. The law states that adaptive complexity becomes favorable when the volatility-driven performance advantage exceeds structural costs, with a critical threshold-Alicia's Threshold-emerging at the 2:1 gain-to-cost ratio. Using 31 years of financial market data from SPY and US Treasury securities (1994-2024), I demonstrate that this threshold manifests precisely in investor behavior. The observed marginal compensation ratio of 2.75 is statistically indistinguishable from the theoretical 2:1 prediction (bootstrap 95% CI for the difference: [-1.54, 7.02], p = 0.74) and validates across 100% of testable business cycle eras. This work establishes that Alicia's Threshold is not merely a statistical artifact but a fundamental organizing principle in financial decision-making under uncertainty.

title: Cyber Laws and Digital Rights in Cameroon: A Critical Analysis of Cybercrime Legislation, Internet Governance, and Freedom of Expression

detail.title: Cyber Laws and Digital Rights in Cameroon: A Critical Analysis of Cybercrime Legislation, Internet Governance, and Freedom of Expression
detail.abstract: This research examines the tension between Cameroon's Cybercrime legislation and the protection of digital rights, particularly freedom of expression and access to information. Using documented cases, media reports, legal texts, and digital rights monitoring data, the study explores how Cybercrime laws have been implemented, how they interact with political dynamics, and the extent to which they contribute to digital authoritarianism. It also analyzes constitutional guarantees, economic consequences, and the broader implications for democratic governance. Recommendations are provided for reform and future research.

title: Stochastic Volatility, Jumps, and Rates: A Unified Framework for Option Pricing and Term-Structure Simulation

detail.title: Stochastic Volatility, Jumps, and Rates: A Unified Framework for Option Pricing and Term-Structure Simulation
detail.abstract: This study develops an integrated stochastic modeling framework for pricing short and medium-maturity equity options and assessing interest-rate risk using the Heston (1993), Bates (1996), and CIR (1985) models. We calibrate the Heston model using both the Lewis (2001) Fourier inversion and the Carr-Madan (1999) FFT approach, finding near-identical parameter sets, which is consistent with the calibration stability reported in recent studies such as Agazzotti et al. (2025). Extending the model to Bates shows that jump intensities converge to values effectively equal to zero for 60-day maturities, echoing empirical findings that jumps contribute marginally to short-term smile fitting. We further compare our calibration approach with the joint volatility-surface and variance-term-structure framework proposed by Yoo (2025), confirming that standard Heston/Bates calibration remains robust for the maturities considered. Finally, we calibrate the CIR short-rate model to the Euribor term structure, generating positive and economically consistent forward-rate scenarios in line with recent stochastic-rate option-pricing research by Jeon and Kim (2025). Overall, our results show that continuous stochastic volatility dominates near-term pricing dynamics, while stochastic interest rates materially influence valuations beyond one year.

title: Beyond Fiat Thinking: A Framework for Systematic Token Accumulation

detail.abstract: The prevailing mindset in crypto is still anchored in fiat thinking: evaluating progress in dollars rather than in quantity accumulation of core assets (ETH/BTC). This paper argues that fiat-denominated thinking is structurally limiting and psychologically destructive. It biases the investor toward shortterm valuation anxiety rather than long-horizon quantity compounding. This paper offers a systematic framework—Systematic Token Accumulation and Cryptocurrency Kit (STACK)—designed to: 1. Escape fiat-denominated evaluation. 2. Optimize token quantity, not portfolio dollar value. 3. Deploy liquidity according to cyclical and structural signals instead of prediction. 4. Use rotations into and out of altcoins strategically to reduce ETH cost basis over time. Core Thesis: Richness is not the number of dollars you have. Richness is ownership of scarce assets that the system cannot print. The sovereign investor accumulates units, not prices.

title: Misery and Prosociality: the Long-run Impact of Early-life Adversity on Prosocial Behavior in China's 1959--1961 Great Famine
affiliations: Jinan University - Institute for Economic and Social Research, University of Oregon, The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) - Department of Economics and Zhejiang University

detail.title: Misery and Prosociality: the Long-run Impact of Early-life Adversity on Prosocial Behavior in China's 1959--1961 Great Famine
detail.abstract: We study the early origins of prosocial behavior by using exogenous exposure to the Great Chinese Famine during early childhood. Using a cohort-based difference-in-differences approach, we find that individuals exposed to the famine between ages 1 and 3 years at its onset exhibit significantly higher charitable donations six decades later. This effect is especially strong for individuals who had siblings during the famine. We provide suggestive evidence that the increase in prosociality is driven by enhanced intra-household interactions during the famine, rather than by income or religiosity effects. These findings highlight the role of family interactions in fostering social altruism, especially in the context of early-life adversity.

title: Democracy Preservation Through Congressional Constitutional Supremacy: An Empirical Framework for Constitutional Crisis Response

detail.title: Democracy Preservation Through Congressional Constitutional Supremacy: An Empirical Framework for Constitutional Crisis Response

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No financial relationships exist that influenced this study.

detail.abstract:
This Article addresses a fundamental and unsettled question in American constitutional law: when do judicial decisions lose democratic legitimacy and require congressional intervention to preserve constitutional democracy? Through application of the Supreme Court's own institutional accountability standards from United States v. Leon, this Article establishes measurable thresholds for determining when courts have systematically abandoned legal methodology in favor of ideological outcome achievement.

Building on Leon's empirical framework for institutional failure—when authority becomes "so lacking in indicia of probable cause as to render official belief in its existence entirely unreasonable"⁵—this Article proposes a novel constitutional crisis response mechanism requiring demonstrable cross-ideological rejection of judicial reasoning before congressional intervention becomes legitimate.

The Leon-based methodology resolves the tension between preserving judicial independence and protecting democracy from judicial capture, providing the first empirical framework for constitutional crisis response grounded in established Supreme Court precedent.

title: Informative Certification and Inefficiency in Trade
affiliations: Free University of Berlin (FUB) - School of Business & Economics,  and Reichman University

detail.title: Informative Certification and Inefficiency in Trade
detail.abstract: This paper studies a model of informative certification in which sellers initially hold soft, partial information about quality and can learn more accurate hard information via certification. We show that a monopolistic certifier may optimally induce trading inefficiency in the market for uncertified goods. The inefficiency is driven either by the certifier's objective to increase the sellers' willingness to pay for certification or the additional adverse selection induced by initially optimistic sellers who enter the uncertified market after learning that their good has low quality. In both instances, trade on the uncertified market is suppressed and most goods are traded with certification.
