detail.title: Oil Price Shocks: Firms' Expectations and Borrowing Decisions
detail.abstract: This paper examines the high-frequency impact of oil price shocks on firms' inflation expectations and subsequent credit demand. Exploiting city-level variation in retail fuel pump prices within a 5-day window, we identify the immediate effect on firms' expectations. Our findings indicate a pass-through of about 30%: a 1 percent increase in local oil prices leads to a 0.3 percentage point rise in firms' one-year-ahead inflation expectations. Building on this, we analyze the consequent shifts in corporate credit behavior following oil supply shocks: a 1 percent increase in fuel prices leads to a 0.5 percent rise in short-term borrowing and a 0.5 percent decline in long-term borrowing, as higher operating costs increase working-capital needs while a weaker macroeconomic outlook reduces planned investment. The net effect is a maturity reallocation rather than a change in total borrowing. The results document a dual channel through which oil shocks shape firms' beliefs and create divergent shifts in short-versus long-term corporate credit demand.

title: Analysis of Data Visualization tools & a Policy and Economic Reflection of the Contemporary Canadian Energy landscape

detail.title: Analysis of Data Visualization tools & a Policy and Economic Reflection of the Contemporary Canadian Energy landscape
detail.abstract: This paper evaluates Canada’s 2023 energy balance and uses it to demonstrate how visualization choices shape policy interpretation. Part A reconciles Statistics Canada’s energy balance with benchmark series from Natural Resources Canada, the Energy Institute, and the IEA. Agreement is strong for total primary supply and for residential, commercial, and transport end-uses, but two branches—industrial consumption and “non-energy” uses—depart from a ±10% consistency rule. I trace these gaps to differences in bookkeeping (e.g., whether fuel burned in power generation is charged to electricity or to industry), inclusion rules for non-energy petroleum feedstocks, time-window and unit-conversion conventions, and the treatment of fossil inputs to electricity that depress modeled generation in some sources. Part B reflects on Canada’s policy position: a hydro- and nuclear-heavy grid, net-exporter status in hydrocarbons, rising investment in LNG and nuclear refurbishments, and the evolving role of carbon pricing and contracts-for-difference amid affordability and reliability constraints. Part C assesses Sankey diagrams as a tool for energy economics—highlighting their strengths in showing systemwide flows and their limits in conveying price dynamics, regional heterogeneity, and uncertainty—then proposes practical checks (timestamping, uncertainty bands, reasonableness screens, and standardized unit conventions). Accurate, well-documented Sankeys materially improve demand, trade, and infrastructure planning in a high-stakes, high-intensity energy system.

title: The Economics of a Just Transition
affiliations: RFF-CMCC European Institute on Economics and the Environment, RFF-CMCC European Institute on Economics and the Environment (EIEE), Mercator Research Institute on Global Commons and Climate Change (MCC), Politecnico di Milano - Department of Management, Economics and Industrial Engineering and University of Milan

detail.title: The Economics of a Just Transition
detail.abstract: Addressing climate change requires policies that are ethically defensible, politically acceptable, and implementable. The concept of a ‘just transition’—a decarbonization process that avoids leaving workers and communities behind and mitigates burdens on vulnerable and historically marginalized groups—has gained prominence in academic and policy debates. This paper bridges these debates with insights from environmental economics. We identify and examine four key dimensions of a just transition—distributional, restorative, procedural, and recognition justice—and use them to map existing economic research. We highlight the contributions and limitations of environmental economics in addressing justice concerns and discuss gaps that future research should address to better inform the design of equitable climate policies.

title: Making the Cut: Close Elections and Local Welfare Policy
affiliations: , Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU) and University of Glasgow - Adam Smith Business School

detail.title: Making the Cut: Close Elections and Local Welfare Policy
detail.abstract: Welfare benefit sanctions are a common tool in many social insurance systems. Using a regression discontinuity design based on close elections, we investigate how representatives’ political alignment influences the implementation of a new sanction regime in the UK. Our results show that constituencies aligned with the Conservative-led central government experience significantly fewer sanctions. The RD estimate indicates a drop of 0.8 percentage points, implying 18 % lower sanction rates in central government controlled constituencies. These findings demonstrate that partisan alignment can systematically shape the local implementation of a national, rule-based policies.

title: Learning the Macroeconomic Language
affiliations: and Saint Louis University - Department of Economics

detail.title: Learning the Macroeconomic Language
detail.abstract: We show how state-of-the-art large language models (LLMs), seemingly inapplicable to the small samples typical of macroeconomics, can be trained effectively for macroeconomic forecasting. We estimate a dynamic stochastic general equilibrium (DSGE) model on an initial segment of the data and obtain a posterior distribution over structural parameters. We sample from this posterior to generate millions of theory-consistent synthetic panels that, when mixed with actual macroeconomic data, form the training corpus for a time-series transformer with attention. The trained model is then used to forecast out-of-sample through 2025. The results show that this hybrid forecaster, which combines the theoretical coherence of DSGE models with the representational power of modern LLMs, learns key features of the macroeconomic language.

title: Solar Adoption by Mandates

detail.title: Solar Adoption by Mandates
detail.abstract: Rooftop solar photovoltaic mandates are becoming a popular policy across Europe and the United States. In this paper, we leverage the frontrunner experience of California to examine their economics. First, we evaluate the private payoffs of solar adoption for residential new construction. To do so, we assemble a rich dataset of new construction building projects and parameterize an engineering model to provide estimates of private payoffs across our sample. Second, we evaluate the hypothesis of what we call a "solar gap'' by comparing the cost-effectiveness estimates from the engineering model to observed builder decisions. We find substantial variation in the cost-effectiveness of solar across building locations and characteristics, though the estimated private payoffs are generally positive across a robust variety of model parameterizations and financial assumptions. We observe that the majority of buildings in our data do not adopt solar despite engineering estimates suggesting opportunities for positive payoffs. Relatedly, we find that payoffs explain little of the variation in solar adoption decisions. Lastly, we estimate the effectiveness of both San Francisco's citywide solar mandate and California's statewide mandate. Across a variety of empirical approaches, we find that both the citywide and statewide mandates increased solar adoption. However, new construction solar adoption remains below 100 percent. We discuss compliance accordingly.

title: From Tweets to Transactions: High-Frequency Inflation Expectations, Consumption, and Stock Returns
affiliations: University Bonn, , Frankfurt School of Finance & Management and Frankfurt School of Finance & Management

detail.title: From Tweets to Transactions: High-Frequency Inflation Expectations, Consumption, and Stock Returns
detail.abstract: Using modern natural language processing, we construct a high-frequency inflation expectations index from German-language tweets. This index closely tracks realized inflation and aligns even more closely with household survey expectations. It also improves short-run forecasts relative to standard benchmarks. In response to monetary policy tightening, the index declines within about a week, with the effects concentrated in tweets by private individuals and during the recent period of elevated inflation. Using 117 million online transactions from German retailers, we show that higher inflation expectations are followed by lower household spending on discretionary goods. By linking these shifts in demand to stock returns, we find that, during periods of elevated inflation, firms operating in discretionary sectors experience significantly lower stock returns when inflation expectations rise. Thus, our Twitter-based index provides market participants and policymakers with a timely tool to monitor inflation sentiment and its economic consequences.

title: Self-enforcing Stable Sets
affiliations: Kobe University and University of Oslo

detail.title: Self-enforcing Stable Sets
detail.abstract: We study coalition formation with externalities under voluntary, non-binding participation. Motivated by climate agreements, where standard modeling predicts small, inefficient coalitions, we propose a new solution concept—the self-enforcing stable set. It synthesizes the self-enforcing logic of non-cooperative approaches with the consistency requirement of cooperative forward-looking stability. By endogenizing players' beliefs about the eventual outcomes of negotiations, we show that rational foresight disciplines strategic free-riding and selects constrained Pareto efficient outcomes. In canonical climate-agreement models, this yields sharp predictions: stable coalitions must be large and only mildly fragmented, aligning closely with observed participation patterns.

title: The Architects of Progress: Strong Institutions Over Strong Leaders

detail.title: The Architects of Progress: Strong Institutions Over Strong Leaders
detail.abstract: This paper examines the long-standing question of whether societal progress is shaped more by exceptional leaders or by the strength of a nation's institutions. Drawing on political philosophy, economic theory, and comparative historical evidence, it argues that durable development rests primarily on the quality and resilience of institutions rather than on the authority of singular "strong men." The discussion traces the evolution of this idea from Hobbes's case for centralized sovereign power to Locke's vision of limited government, rule of law, and constitutional checks. It then connects these philosophical foundations to modern institutional economics, particularly the distinction between inclusive and extractive institutions that shape incentives, innovation, and long-run growth. Using case studies from Africa and Asia-including Botswana, Ghana, Zimbabwe, South Korea, Singapore, and China. The paper shows how institutional strength or weakness predicts divergent development paths, even where resources, culture, or leadership appear similar. While acknowledging that powerful leaders can catalyze short-term reforms, the analysis demonstrates that such gains rarely endure without strong legal, political, and administrative systems to support them. The conclusion emphasizes that sustainable progress requires strengthening governance structures, embedding accountability, and ensuring that laws, not personalities, govern political and economic life.

title: Theory of Economic Stablility

detail.title: Theory of Economic Stablility
detail.abstract: Humanity has long sought a stable foundation for money - from gold to fiat currencies, from Bitcoin to modern stablecoins - yet each has failed to end the cycle of inflation, crashes, and inequality. At the root of these failures is a flawed assumption: pegging money to external assets or political will cannot create lasting stability. This paper introduces MVPQ, a groundbreaking monetary framework that dynamically governs both price stability and monetary velocity, while redirecting surplus growth or reserve for future capacity and adaption at a given velocity for an ecological aware planet. By addressing the causes of instability rather than its symptoms, MVPQ creates the first true stablecoin - one that neither inflates nor deflates - providing a transparent, self-regulating system capable of supporting sustainable prosperity for all.  Constituted by the Law of Economic Thermodynamics:  PQ = Σ(MV) + Δ(M_FAC × V_FAC) and ΔFAC = PQ – MV

detail.abstract: Enhanced security threats in wartime and post-crisis environments that require systemic resilience and the protection of national interests entail implementing national institutional, informational, legal, and human resources to their fullest capabilities. In so doing, it offers an unparalleled overview of the organizational, legal, informational, and human factors within public management that shape the performance of the national security system. This paper articulates and theorizes central principles for constructing a modern national security system featuring a hierarchy of national interests, multi-level state, sub-state, and non-state actor coordination, transparency, and attunement to global best practices. Utilizing NCSI as an empirical reference frame, the paper discusses the transformation of cybersecurity and digital preparedness capabilities among EU members for the period 2023-2025, displaying a longer-term view of increasing cyclicality of cyber resilience across the European security architecture. Strategic implications: the study suggests that the IIS's evolution must be based on a synergy of technological innovation, sound legal regulation, and competent human resources. The structure and processes of national security governance, therefore, need to be transformed into strategic decentralization, interinstitutional cooperation, and digital inclusion. The findings advance the theory and practice of the impact of digital transformation on national security governance mechanisms and provide conceptual premises for improving public management strategies in an age of globalization and technological convergence.

title: A Multidimensional Scaling Analysis of Statistical Index Construction Using Major Economic Indicators in the Philippines

detail.title: A Multidimensional Scaling Analysis of Statistical Index Construction Using Major Economic Indicators in the Philippines

contentType.other: This work is a thesis/project submitted in 2025, archived in Zenodo with DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.17587302

detail.abstract: Economists have formulated different kinds of indexes that assess development. So far, Human Development Index (HDI) is the only existing composite index for every province in the Philippines that measures the basic dimensions of development and has been criticized on a number of grounds including the measurement error of the underlying statistical method which leads to a severe misclassification in the ranking of development. Considering this, the aim of this study was to construct an alternative measure of a region’s economic performance using economic indicators. The variables that were considered in the study are the 10 selected economic indicators used by the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) for monitoring progress of the economy in 17 regions in the Philippines. The analysis of data considered only a time frame of 10 years. Variables then underwent standardization to address measurement units. Standardized variables were subjected to multidimensional scaling (MDS) analysis to place each variable in 2-dimensional space while the between-variable distances were preserved as well as possible. The highest stress-tested coordinate in every variable were collected and used in the construction of the statistical index, the Economic Development Index (EDI), of a particular region in the Philippines. Bootstrap resampling was performed to check the statistical properties of the constructed indices such as unbiasedness and consistency. On the other hand, provincial HDI were being ranked carefully. The rankings of the EDI and the HDI were comprehensively presented. Based on the findings, Region 4-A: CALABARZON got the highest EDI value of 30.76581% while region 1: ILOCOS REGION got the lowest EDI value of 27.49474%. And for the provincial HDI, Manila got the highest value of 83.7% and Sulu got the lowest value of 27.6%. Evidently, the Economic Development Index (EDI) was found to possess desirable statistical characteristic of a good estimator.

title: From Situational Rhetoric to Systemic Reality: Alliance Dynamics and Economic Restructuring in the Post-Hegemonic Era

detail.title: From Situational Rhetoric to Systemic Reality: Alliance Dynamics and Economic Restructuring in the Post-Hegemonic Era
detail.abstract: This study introduces the concept of "situational clamoring" to explain how defensive political rhetoric triggers rapid alliance deterioration in economically interdependent relationships. We define situational clamoring as defensive independence statements made by leaders under ally pressure. While such rhetoric appears contextual, it creates cascading economic realignments. We test this framework using Netanyahu's 2024-2025 statements and subsequent global responses. Spain canceled $1.35 billion in defense contracts following Netanyahu's "stand alone" declaration. His "Super-Sparta" economic model accelerated European distancing. These patterns validate our theoretical predictions. The findings show that in financially interdependent alliances, rhetorical events function as reliability signals. Partners rationally reassess economic vulnerabilities and seek alternatives. This creates self-reinforcing cycles of partnership deterioration. Our framework bridges political communication and alliance theory, explaining contemporary alliance fragmentation through the interaction of rhetoric and economic interdependence.

title: Urban Distribution of Older Adults: Concentration and Socio-Spatial Typologies in Santiago, Chile

detail.title: Urban Distribution of Older Adults: Concentration and Socio-Spatial Typologies in Santiago, Chile
detail.abstract: Although previous studies have examined the spatial distribution of the aging population in various regions of the world, a significant knowledge gap remains regarding South America. This research aims to address the accelerated demographic change towards an older urban population in cities that have not been planned for this shift and have not developed adaptive urban planning strategies. Socioeconomic and spatial typologies that influence urban aging trajectories in Santiago, Chile, were identified using three methods: geospatial analysis, a data panel, and k-means clustering analysis. It was found that there is a shift in the areas of concentration of older adults, from central to peripheral communes, and that variables such as single-parent families, population density, and high educational levels are factors that increase the concentration of older adults at a communal level. In contrast, homeownership has a negative influence.

detail.abstract: Sari-sari stores serve as vital pillars of rural economies in Northern Mindanao, providing essential goods, local employment, and fostering social cohesion within communities. Despite their significance, many of these microenterprises face enduring challenges, including limited access to capital, weak financial management, and competition from larger retail chains. Ensuring their sustainability is therefore crucial for supporting inclusive rural development. However, limited empirical research has examined localized strategies that promote the long-term growth of these stores across rural Mindanao, creating a notable research gap. This paper explores the demographic characteristics and sustainable growth strategies of sari-sari store owners in rural locality in Northern Mindanao focusing on financial performance, customer retention, and community engagement. A quantitative descriptive design was employed, surveying store owners through a structured questionnaire and analyzing data using descriptive statistics such as frequency, percentage, and mean. Findings indicate that store ownership is predominantly female and concentrated among older adults who exhibit strong financial discipline, community ties, and customer-oriented service. Nonetheless, challenges remain in innovation, income disparity, and cautiousness in offering credit. The results underscore the importance of capacity-building initiatives, financial literacy programs, and youth entrepreneurship engagement to enhance resilience and competitiveness. These insights contribute to the formulation of policies supporting financial inclusion and sustainable rural enterprise development in Northern Mindanao.

The findings suggest that dynamics of work-related values cannot be assumed to be a factor explaining the long run dynamics of labor supply based on this applied measurement framework.

detail.abstract: This paper evaluates Bihar's 2030 development model through an economics framework, focusing on growth strategy, labour-market dynamics, public investment patterns, and institutional constraints. The analysis highlights three central components of the model: (i) large-scale employment generation, targeting one crore new opportunities by 2030; (ii) accelerated public infrastructure spending to stimulate long-run productivity; and (iii) sectoral interventions aimed at raising human capital and attracting private investment. Using recent budget data, labour trends, and sectoral growth indicators, the paper assesses whether the proposed policy mix is consistent with Bihar's structural characteristics-low per-capita income, high dependence on migration, limited industrial base, and modest fiscal capacity. The findings suggest that while the development blueprint has the potential to shift Bihar toward a higher growth path, its success hinges on complementary reforms: improving state capacity, strengthening market institutions, enhancing skill formation, and crowding in private capital. The paper concludes that without these enabling conditions, Bihar's 2030 targets risk remaining aspirational rather than achievable.

detail.abstract: This paper explores and examines the key factors as to why the U.S. dollar has had a recent surge in strength worldwide. Basic macroeconomic concepts, such as supply-and-demand, inflation trends, and global trade will be used to explain this. The findings in this paper come from recent reports from sources like the Federal Reserve, World Bank Open, Trading Economics, and more. title: A Structural Theory of Value: Dissipation, Boundaries, and System Performance

detail.title: A Structural Theory of Value: Dissipation, Boundaries, and System Performance
detail.abstract: All real systems transform inputs into outputs while producing dissipation. Some systems maintain performance reliably; others accumulate friction, redundancy, and structural drag. Despite the universality of these patterns, no cross-domain framework exists for explaining why systems diverge so widely in performance or how they can be systematically improved. This paper presents a structural theory of value, distinguishing between unavoidable dissipation, imposed by a system's environment, and avoidable dissipation, which arises from misalignment, unnecessary complexity, and coordination overhead. A system creates value when it reduces avoidable dissipation while fulfilling the requirements that define its boundary and purpose within the chosen analytical frame. The theory introduces a dimensional decomposition of improvement into three structural levers-Sophistication, Simplification, and Scale-which together describe how systems increase capability, reduce friction, or distribute cost. It clarifies the role of boundary validity, distinguishes exploratory waste from structural inefficiency, and explains how slack contributes to resilience. Applications across biology, computation, organizations, markets, and engineering demonstrate the framework's generality. By focusing on dissipation structure rather than subjective preference or price, the Structural Theory of Value offers a general systems method for diagnosing inefficiency, guiding redesign, and understanding how complex systems grow, stagnate, or collapse.

detail.abstract: This research examines the phenomenon of public debt in the Republic of Moldova, focusing on its emergence, drivers, and implications. Since gaining independence in 1991, Moldova has relied on public debt to stabilize its economy during significant transitions and crises. The aim of this study is to analyze the evolution of the Republic of Moldova's debt, using historical and macroeconomic data to identify patterns and assess its socioeconomic impacts. Key events, including the 2008-2009 global financial crisis, the 2014 "Theft of the century", the COVID-19 pandemic, and the ongoing energy crisis, are central to understanding the country's debt trajectory. The methodology involves a review of governmental fiscal reports, IMF and World Bank data, and secondary sources analyzing the Republic of Moldova's economic policies and crises. Quantitative analysis of debt-to-GDP ratios, fiscal deficits, and debt servicing costs complements a qualitative assessment of policy decisions and structural challenges. Findings indicate that the Republic of Moldova's public debt has consistently risen in response to economic shocks, structural inefficiencies, and geopolitical tensions. Debt reached nearly 40% of GDP by 2024, driven by increased borrowing to address energy price spikes, pandemic recovery, and social support measures. While public debt has enabled crucial investments, it raises concerns about sustainability, governance, and economic resilience. Challenges include diminishing fiscal flexibility, escalating repayment obligations, and the potential erosion of public trust. The study concludes that prudent fiscal strategies, economic diversification, and governance reforms are essential to ensure that public debt supports sustainable development while minimizing long-term risks to the population.

detail.title: Does Investor Attention Drive the Connectedness across FX, Bond, Stock, and Commodity Markets? Evidence from the Federal Funds Rate
detail.abstract: This study examines how investor attention to the “federal funds rate” influences return spillovers across foreign exchange, bond, stock, and commodity markets. Our framework can be categorized into two segments. First, we utilize a time-varying parameter vector autoregressive connectedness model to estimate the dynamic spillover effect across these markets from 2004 to 2025; we then employ Google search volume as a proxy for investor attention and regress it on connectedness indices to evaluate the influence of attention. Our findings suggest that increased attention significantly reduces the total connectedness index, indicating that attention can improve market efficiency. Second, it shows the same influence on the total directional connectedness of the stock and commodity markets, helping stabilize shocks that flow into and out of both markets. However, the impact of investor attention on spillovers during different crises is heterogeneous, depending on the specific conditions at the moment. These findings highlight the role of investor attention in cross-market risk contagion and suggest that policymakers monitor attention indicators and enhance investor communication to reduce information asymmetry.

title: Range-Clearing: A Market-Structure Analysis Framework Based on Intervals and Covariance

detail.title: Range-Clearing: A Market-Structure Analysis Framework Based on Intervals and Covariance
detail.abstract: This paper challenges the efficient-market hypothesis (EMH) at its epistemological root by replacing its "point equilibrium" microfoundation with a more realistic framework termed "range-clearing." We argue that subjective value is not a precise point but a range of acceptability, and that market transactions clear not at a singular price but within a zone of overlapping value ranges. From this single premise, a fundamental re-evaluation of market efficiency emerges. We demonstrate, first, that the market’s apparent "stickiness" or hesitation to react to minor informational stimuli is not a sign of inefficiency, but is instead the hallmark of a higher-order cognitive efficiency, whereby rational actors conserve scarce mental resources by strategically ignoring noise that falls within their acceptance range. Second, we show that this mechanism structurally ensures that the market functions as a low-pass information filter, systematically and rationally culling high-frequency "noise" at each transactional node. This finding renders the strong and semi-strong forms of EMH ontologically impossible, as the market price cannot, even in theory, reflect "all" available information. By reconceptualizing the market not as a flawless information-processing machine but as a profoundly human institution of cognitive economizing and selective judgment, this paper provides a robust, rational explanation for real-world phenomena such as price momentum and financial crashes. We conclude that EMH is not so much incorrect as it is a special, and unrealistic, case of our more general theory, and call for a paradigm shift in financial economics—away from the sterile mechanics of informational efficiency and toward a more fruitful science of human judgment in an uncertain world.

title: Foreign Exchange Risk Management: Hedging vs. Natural Hedging

detail.title: Foreign Exchange Risk Management: Hedging vs. Natural Hedging
detail.abstract:
Foreign exchange (FX) risk is one of the most significant financial challenges faced by firms engaged in international operations. Fluctuations in currency values directly affect cash flows, profitability, competitiveness, and firm valuation. This paper examines the nature and drivers of FX risk, the forms of currency exposure, and the comparative effectiveness of financial hedging and natural hedging as risk-management strategies. Financial hedging relies on derivatives such as forwards, futures, options, and swaps, offering precision and flexibility but at a cost. Natural hedging, in contrast, restructures operational activities—such as matching currency inflows and outflows or borrowing in foreign currency—to reduce exposure with minimal financial expense.

The study integrates theoretical perspectives from the Modigliani–Miller (M&M) theorem and Agency Theory to explain why hedging becomes value-relevant in real-world markets characterized by taxes, transaction costs, and information asymmetry. The paper argues that an optimal FX risk-management framework often combines both natural and financial hedging to enhance stability, reduce volatility, and align managerial decisions with shareholder interests. The findings offer practical insight for students, early researchers, and firms seeking a foundational understanding of FX risk management.

title: The Impact of Multigrade Classes on Student Achievement in Canada

detail.title: The Impact of Multigrade Classes on Student Achievement in Canada
detail.abstract: Objective Multi-grade classes represent an instructional model in which students from different grade levels share the same classroom. In a context where the empirical effects of this pedagogical arrangement remain scarcely documented in Canada, the present study aims to evaluate the impact of multi-grade classes on the academic achievement of third-grade students in Ontario. Methods Using publicly available school-level aggregated data, two evaluation approaches are employed to account for the potential endogeneity of the number of students in multi-grade classes. The first method, an instrumental variable regression, relies on a prediction rule for the number of students in multi-grade classes, based on third-grade enrollment figures and considering the discontinuities observed at thresholds corresponding to the maximum regulated class size for third grade or its multiples. The second method, a regression discontinuity design, directly exploits these discontinuities in the distribution of students across multi-grade classes. A difference-indifferences version of this method further allows for a more rigorous consideration of unobservable differences around the discontinuity thresholds. Results The results obtained from these methods indicate that multi-grade classes exert an adverse effect on academic achievement. Moreover, the magnitude of these negative effects increases with the number of third-grade students who share their learning environment with students from adjacent grade levels.

title: The Effects of Monetary Policy in Sweden During the Inflation Targeting Period: Estimates with Structural VAR Models

detail.title: The Effects of Monetary Policy in Sweden During the Inflation Targeting Period: Estimates with Structural VAR Models
detail.abstract: In this staff memo, we present estimates of the effects of monetary policy in Sweden over the inflation targeting period, from 1995 to the end of 2022, with structural vector autoregressive (SVAR) models and short-run restrictions to identify the monetary policy shocks. This is a common method for calculating the effects of monetary policy, and it is one of several approaches used by the Riksbank. However, research studies on Swedish data using similar approaches were typically done 10-20 years ago and we now have considerably more data for the inflation targeting period, which makes it timely to update previous estimates and document the new results. Our estimated effects of monetary policy on GDP are slightly larger than in previous studies on Swedish data, while the effects on inflation are in line with previous studies. We show that the effects on CPIF inflation have been stable over time, while the effects on GDP, housing investment, consumption, house prices and household debt have probably increased over time. These observations could be explained by various structural changes that have increased household indebtedness and made the Swedish economy more interest-rate sensitive during the inflation targeting period. The fact that the effects of monetary policy on inflation have not become larger despite larger effects on the real economy could be due to the fact that the sensitivity of prices to changes in costs has simultaneously decreased, i.e. the Phillips curve has become flatter. On the contrary, during the inflation surge in 2022, data indicate that businesses have raised their prices more than usual relative to how costs have evolved, but this short period has no visible impact on our calculations. There is considerable uncertainty about the effects of monetary policy and the estimated effects are affected by a number of different assumptions. It is important to highlight this uncertainty and to discuss the plausibility of various assumptions made. We therefore devote a relatively large amount of space to sensitivity analyses that highlight local model uncertainty, i.e. uncertainty within the framework of the SVAR model. This analysis can also guide other studies of the effects of monetary policy with similar methods. Our calculations are part of the Riksbank’s overall assessment of the effects of monetary policy. Different methods yield slightly different results and the study can therefore not be interpreted as the Riksbank’s overall assessment of the effects of monetary policy on the Swedish economy. The Riksbank’s forecasts and analyses include a number of other factors that, in different situations, influence the assessment of the pass-through of monetary policy.

title: The Imaginary Unit as the Financial Imaginary: A Philosophical and Mathematical Justification for the Role of i in Modeling Credit-Driven Economies

detail.title: The Imaginary Unit as the Financial Imaginary: A Philosophical and Mathematical Justification for the Role of i in Modeling Credit-Driven Economies
detail.abstract: We argue that the imaginary unit i acquires genuine economic interpretability in modern leverage-driven economies precisely because private credit has evolved into an autonomous, cyclically misaligned subsystem relative to real production. While pure exponential credit growth requires only real exponentials, the observed combination of (a) super-exponential credit trends, (b) medium-term financial cycles, and (c) persistent phase misalignment between credit and real activity demands a complex-valued representation Z(t) = R(t) + i C(t). Euler's formula then naturally generates logarithmic spirals in the complex plane whose geometric properties-expansion rate b = (γ-ζ)/ω and imbalance angle θ(t) ≈ C(t)/R(t)-directly map onto Minskyan fragility and early-warning signals. Drawing on recent empirical complex-plane models (2024-2025), we show that this representation is not merely convenient but mathematically minimal and empirically superior. The imaginary axis thereby ceases to be "imaginary" in the pejorative sense: in a debt-money economy, credit literally occupies an orthogonal dimension to real output, and i becomes the coordinate that makes that orthogonality visible.

title: Switching between States and the COVID-19 Turbulence

detail.title: Switching between States and the COVID-19 Turbulence
detail.abstract: In Aarab (2020), I examine U.S. stock return predictability across economic regimes and document evidence of time-varying expected returns across market states in the long run. The analysis introduces a state-switching specification in which the market state is proxied by the slope of the yield curve, and proposes an Aligned Economic Index built from the popular predictors of Welch and Goyal (2008) (augmented with bond and equity premium measures). The Aligned Economic Index under the state-switching model exhibits statistically and economically meaningful in-sample (R 2 = 5.9%) and out-of-sample (R 2 oos = 4.12%) predictive power across both recessions and expansions, while outperforming a range of widely used predictors. In this work, I examine the added value for professional practitioners by computing the economic gains for a mean-variance investor and find substantial added benefit of using the new index under the state switching model across all market states. The Aligned Economic Index can thus be implemented on a consistent real-time basis. These findings are crucial for both academics and practitioners as expansions are much longer-lived than recessions. Finally, I extend the empirical exercises by incorporating data through September 2020 and document sizable gains from using the Aligned Economic Index, relative to more traditional approaches, during the COVID-19 market turbulence.

title: Duality and Recursion in Dynamic Games

detail.title: Duality and Recursion in Dynamic Games
detail.abstract: This paper develops dual recursive methods to study dynamic games with imperfect monitoring. It begins by defining two kinds of perfect public equilibrium that exploit communication differently, then formulates sequence problems that realize their welfare as linear programs. Their value functions are equated to maximal fixed points of corresponding functional equations defined by convex programs, with implied dual functional equations amenable to computation. In games with frequent actions, this yields welfare optimality (HJB) equations that relate the curvature of welfare to welfare itself. I apply these results to the repeated Prisoners' Dilemma, optimal dynamic contracting and approximate equilibrium.

title: Automorphic Neural Theory: The First Framework for 'Homeostatic Intelligence' via Introspective Topology Rewriting
affiliations: Dr Akhilesh Das Gupta Institute of Professional Studies

detail.title: Automorphic Neural Theory: The First Framework for 'Homeostatic Intelligence' via Introspective Topology Rewriting

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no conflicts of interest. This research was conducted independently, with no financial, personal, or organizational relationships that could be perceived as influencing the work.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve human participants, animals, or sensitive data. Therefore, ethics approval and informed consent were not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. The work was completed independently without financial support from any institution, organization, or sponsor.

detail.abstract: For most of its history, connectionism has relied on one basic assumption: the structure of a neural network is chosen beforehand and never changes. Whether we train a tiny Perceptron or a huge LLM, the number of layers, the size of each layer, and the wiring between them are all fixed by engineers. Once training begins, only the weights (θ) move, while the topology (G) stays frozen. This Static Topology Assumption creates two major problems: simple networks can't represent complex patterns, and oversized networks waste energy and easily overfit. In this work, I question this assumption directly. I introduce Automorphic Neural Theory (ANT), a framework that treats the topology G as something that can change and learn-just like the weights-giving the network the ability to reshape itself while it trains.

title: Forward-Jump Random Walks on a Finite Cycle with Laziness and Teleportation: Hitting Times, Mixing, and Cutoff
affiliations: Rajamangala University of Technology Suvarnabhumi, Heriot-Watt University and Dhonburi Rajabhat University

detail.title: Forward-Jump Random Walks on a Finite Cycle with Laziness and Teleportation: Hitting Times, Mixing, and Cutoff
detail.abstract: We introduce a translation-invariant random walk on a finite cycle that integrates three fundamental mechanisms: random step increments, laziness (a stay-put move), and teleportation (a reset to a uniformly chosen position). Since the resulting transition kernel is circulant, discrete Fourier analysis provides an explicit characterization of the spectrum. Leveraging this spectral structure, we derive a finite Fourier-series representation of the time-n distribution and, via a renewal identity and generating-function techniques, obtain closed-form expressions for the mean and variance of the first hitting time of an arbitrary target state. The same Fourier-based approach yields sharp bounds on the mixing behavior and the spectral gap, and it delineates broad parameter regimes in which no total-variation cutoff occurs. In the presence of teleportation, we further establish an exact decomposition implying dimension-free geometric convergence to stationarity, together with an explicit exponential tail bound for hitting times. Finally, numerical experiments and a board-game proxy illustrate how the step distribution, laziness, and teleportation parameters jointly determine pacing, variability, and fairness.

title: The Impact of Construal-Level Manipulation on Real and Hypothetical Self-Control Outcomes
affiliations: Penn State Altoona and Penn State Altoona

detail.title: The Impact of Construal-Level Manipulation on Real and Hypothetical Self-Control Outcomes
detail.abstract: Self-control plays a central role in health-related decision-making. This is particularly true for dietary behaviors which often involve conflicts between tempting and healthy food choices. Construal-level theory (CLT) suggests that thinking globally (in terms of superordinate goals, or “why”) promotes self-control, while thinking locally (in terms of subordinate means, or “how”) encourages immediate gratification. Although prior research indicates that construal-level manipulations influence hypothetical outcomes such as delay discounting and snack choice intentions, limited work has examined their effects on real-world behavior. The present study investigated whether the Why-How construal manipulation impacts both hypothetical and actual dietary self-control outcomes. Eighty-nine undergraduates were randomly assigned to a global or local construal condition before completing a hypothetical delay discounting task and a real snack food choice. Manipulation checks confirmed successful induction of global versus local construal. Consistent with hypotheses, participants in the global condition demonstrated greater self-control on the delay discounting task, evidenced by significantly lower discounting rates. Regarding real behavior, participants in the global condition were marginally more likely to select a healthy snack relative to those in the local condition. These results suggest that inducing global construal may be a promising tool for bolstering self-control, particularly in the context of dietary decision-making. Future research should explore boundary conditions, including individual differences and readiness to change, to clarify the potential of CLT-based interventions for health behavior change.

title: Cognitive Field Dynamics: A Unified Theory of Consciousness, Expectation, and Experiential Geometry

detail.title: Cognitive Field Dynamics: A Unified Theory of Consciousness, Expectation, and Experiential Geometry

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest. This research was conducted independently without external funding, commercial affiliations, or financial relationships that could be perceived to have influenced the work.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This is a theoretical paper presenting a conceptual framework. No human participants, patients, or empirical data collection were involved in this research.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. This work was independently conducted and self-funded by the author through the LifePillar Institute.

detail.abstract: This paper presents Cognitive Field Dynamics (CFD), a unified theory of consciousness integrating four complementary frameworks: (1) a nine-layer cognitive architecture spanning from prereflective awareness to behavioral expression; (2) an Expectation Framework specifying the directional mechanics of anticipatory cognition through a 32-point compass, temporal operators, temporal gradients, and pressure dynamics; (3) a 57-qubit information-theoretic basis establishing the minimal dimensionality of human experiential state-space at 1.73 × 1017 distinguishable configurations; and (4) a collapse-reset temporal architecture identifying 12.5 Hz as the recursive identity update frequency and the sleep cycle as the fundamental harmonic governor. The theory proposes that consciousness is a field that organizes physical reality through expectation-biased collapse of possibility into actuality. The 57-qubit basis represents the interface resolution through which consciousness specifies its output to shared reality. The 32-point expectation compass describes the directional structure of this biasing process. Temporal operators describe how consciousness shapes temporal experience. The sleep cycle provides the metarecursive reset required for system stability. The unified architecture generates testable predictions across physiological, cognitive, behavioral, and societal levels, with preliminary empirical validation through the Psychosocial Pressure Index (PPI). The framework establishes Cognitive Field Dynamics as a distinct scientific discipline with applications in clinical psychology, organizational dynamics, and population-level forecasting.

title: An Analysis of the Indian Laws and Policies addressing Historical Injustice with Local Communities and Deforestation for Sustainable Forestry

detail.title: An Analysis of the Indian Laws and Policies addressing Historical Injustice with Local Communities and Deforestation for Sustainable Forestry
detail.abstract: Forests were managed by the local communities in India and forests possess the characteristics of substractability and non-excludability making them common property resources. However, with the Britishers denied the local communities with access to forest lands due to the doctrine of Terra Nullius. It was assumed that state-control will reduce degradation but it continued. Subsequently, many scholars debated for community management of forests to achieve sustainable forestry. Based on such ideology, regulations were adopted in many countries and in India too, laws for addressing historical injustice with the local communities and improving the forest health were adopted. However, issues of determination of local people and their rights could not be solved adequately. Therefore, study of such regulations becomes important. This paper thus analyzes those Indian legislations to understand the gap between the allocation of rights to the local forest dwellers and the achievement of sustainable forestry.

title: Moutai's Dilemma and Breakthrough: Value Anchoring Amid Cyclical Fluctuations

detail.title: Moutai's Dilemma and Breakthrough: Value Anchoring Amid Cyclical Fluctuations
detail.abstract: At the end of 2025, the price of the overseas version of 53% vol Feitian Moutai nearly matched its stock price, reflecting Moutai's cyclical dilemma amid policy controls, weak demand, and high inventory. Looking back at history, Moutai has navigated five fluctuations by virtue of brand barriers, scarce supply, and channel reforms. Currently, the industry is experiencing intensified differentiation, while positive policy signals and consumption structure transformation are bringing new opportunities. Moutai is breaking through by deepening direct sales reforms, optimizing product structure, and expanding diversified consumption scenarios. In the short term, the focus is on price stabilization and inventory destocking; in the long run, its core value logic remains unchanged. The cyclical bottom is precisely a key window for its value reshaping.

title: The Logic of the Market: Planning Games, Responsibility Alignment, and Forced Equilibrium

detail.title: The Logic of the Market: Planning Games, Responsibility Alignment, and Forced Equilibrium
detail.abstract: This paper proposes a market theory centered on an integrated sequence-institutional platform → planning games → Responsibility Alignment → forced equilibrium-to explain why market outcomes frequently deviate from the self-adjusting, welfare-optimal equilibrium presumed in mainstream economics. The paper argues that a market is not merely a pricecoordination device. Rather, it is an institutionally constituted platform of explicit and implicit rules, within which individuals, firms, and governments continuously formulate plans, interact strategically, revise beliefs, and exit when plans become unsustainable. In this view, the "invisible hand" is an emergent outcome of decentralized planning interactions and feedback, whose effectiveness depends on platform quality-especially the degree to which a system enforces Responsibility Alignment, i.e., whether decision-makers bear consequences commensurate with the power and benefits they enjoy. Building on this foundation, the paper introduces the concept of forced equilibrium: equilibrium is often not a voluntary, preferencedriven Walrasian outcome, but a stage-wise stability produced under institutional and monetary constraints through the compelled exit of unsustainable plans. Destructive adjustments-such as inflation, deflation, unemployment, and bankruptcy-constitute typical implementation mechanisms. The paper therefore redefines the role of government as both a provider of institutional infrastructure and a macro-planning agent responsible for stabilization and crisis relief, while allowing conditional industrial policy for directional experimentation. Government effectiveness, however, hinges on institutional arrangements that are constrainable, testable, and corrigible. The proposed framework offers an operational pathway for analyzing market failure, the boundary conditions of macroeconomic policy, and principles of institutional design.

title: A Structural Break in the UST Relative Safety Premium After the 2022 Russian Reserve Seizure

detail.title: A Structural Break in the UST Relative Safety Premium After the 2022 Russian Reserve Seizure
detail.abstract: This project investigates whether the global financial system experienced a fundamental change in the pricing of U.S. Treasury securities during periods of market stress following the 2022 seizure of Russian central bank reserves by the United States and its allies. Using high-frequency yield data from 20 countries and an event-study design centered on VIX spikes, the analysis uncovers a statistically and economically significant structural break in the U.S. Treasury relative safety premium—a break that reverses the traditional safe-haven behavior of U.S. long-term yields.

title: Climate Change Risks, ESG Disclosure, and Disinvestment: Evidence from Cross-shareholdings

detail.title: Climate Change Risks, ESG Disclosure, and Disinvestment: Evidence from Cross-shareholdings

declarations.funderStatement: This research was supported by a grant-in-aid from JSPS KAKENHI Grant Number JP24K04958.

detail.abstract: We investigate the effect of firms' climate change risk on the disinvestment behavior of firms' cross-shareholders. Using Japanese firm shareholder-matched data, we show that firms with high CO2 intensity experience disinvestment by their business partners. Shareholders' disinvestment behavior toward climate-risky firms is evident when shareholders' ESG scores are high, they are major shareholders, and both firms and shareholders are brown industries. We also find that the effect of firms' climate risk is curbed when firms are stable long-term suppliers with high market power and they also own shareholders' share. Our findings indicate that shareholders consider the climate risk of their business partners and mitigate the future downside risks of their investment assets. However, the effect of firms' climate riskiness is limited by the nature of their business relationships each other.

title: GDELT Successor Project: “K-N-GDELT”

detail.title: GDELT Successor Project: “K-N-GDELT”
detail.abstract: In June of this year, GDELT (www.gdeltproject.org) went silent without notice or explanation. Until that time, GDELT had been a pillar of the OSINT (Open Source Intelligence) community. Rooted in DARPA research, and leaning on work by Philip Schrodt and Andy Halterman and the legendary TABARI & PETRARCH event coding ecosystem, GDELT took on the challenge to model the globe --- the kind of which was previously reserved for state actors and intelligence agencies. The GDELT dataset had proven immensely useful. As we enter a geopolitically more turbulent era, we can no longer take GDELT for granted. At Karmaflows, this inspired us to re-write GDELT from scratch, an odyssey that we vastly under-appreciated at its onset. We named the project K-N-GDELT which stands for “Karmaflows is Not GDELT.” We are happy to announce that 4 months later, we have substantially completed K-N-GDELT.

title: Pensions and Gender in Mexico: Effects of Labor Trajectories on Accumulated Savings
affiliations: Universidad Autonoma de Nuevo Leon and Universidad Autónoma de Tamaulipas

detail.title: Pensions and Gender in Mexico: Effects of Labor Trajectories on Accumulated Savings
detail.abstract: This research analyzes gender gaps in retirement savings in Mexico, using the 2015 Labor Trajectories Survey as a basis and Monte Carlo method simulations. Differentiated labor trajectories between men and women are examined, as well as their impact on the accumulation of pension savings. The study shows that women face structural disadvantages due to labor interruptions, lower contribution density, and lower incomes, which negatively affect the amount accumulated for retirement. The results indicate that there is a highly significant difference between the mean accumulated retirement savings of men and women, and that women's savings could represent only 46.6% of those of men. The study highlights the need to design public policies that incorporate a gender perspective in order to reduce economic inequalities in old age.

title: Financial Innovation and the Stock Price Crash Risk of Technology Firms: Evidence from a Quasi-Natural Experiment in the Sci-Tech Finance Reform Pilot Zones
affiliations: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen and China Securities Regulatory Commission

detail.title: Financial Innovation and the Stock Price Crash Risk of Technology Firms: Evidence from a Quasi-Natural Experiment in the Sci-Tech Finance Reform Pilot Zones
detail.abstract: In recent years, China has continuously strengthened financial support for technologybased enterprises. Using A-share listed firms from 2017 to 2024 as the sample, this study exploits the establishment of the Sci-Tech Finance Reform Pilot Zones as a quasi-natural experiment and employs a difference-indifferences approach to examine the impact of financial innovation on the stock price crash risk of technology firms. The empirical results show that the establishment of the pilot zones significantly reduces the stock price crash risk of local technology firms. Further mechanism analysis reveals that this mitigating effect is more pronounced among firms with financing difficulties or relatively sound corporate governance. These findings indicate that various financial innovations within the pilot zones enhance the accessibility and convenience of financial resources, effectively alleviating the financing difficulties and high financing costs faced by technology firms. Additionally, financial resources flow toward technology firms with stronger corporate governance, reflecting the targeted characteristics of policy implementation. This study also finds that the level of regional financial development influences policy effectiveness. These results provide empirical evidence of the actual effects of financial innovation and offer references for the future expansion of related policies.

title: The Effect of Public Expenditures Composition on Promoting Morocco’s Economic Growth
affiliations: Ibn Tofail University, Ibn Tofail University, Ibn Tofail University and Ibn Tofail University

detail.title: The Effect of Public Expenditures Composition on Promoting Morocco’s Economic Growth
detail.abstract: Public expenditures are an essential component of economic policy. It is used by governments as an operational tool to promote strong, sustainable growth, in particular to achieve the various sustainable development goals. This article aims to examine the effect of the composition of public expenditure on economic growth in Morocco. This subject is becoming increasingly important, as we consider that productive public expenditures have a lasting influence on the economy's growth rate. We have chosen a quantitative approach, using an econometric study. Our research methodology employs the Autoregressive Distributed Lag Bounds testing approach to identify the short-term and long-term effects of public expenditures composition on promoting economic growth. The results revealed a positive but statistically insignificant long-term effect on investment expenditure, as well as on external debt expenditure and savings. Our results also showed a positive and statistically significant impact of operating expenditures, as well as expenditures on goods and services, and trade openness. However, compensation expenditure had an adverse effect.  These results allow us to distinguish between productive and non-productive expenditure during the study period.

title: Geopolitical Risk in the Euro Area: Measurement and Transmission
affiliations: Deutsche Bundesbank, Deutsche Bundesbank, Research Centre, Deutsche Bundesbank - Research Centre and Deutsche Bundesbank

detail.title: Geopolitical Risk in the Euro Area: Measurement and Transmission
detail.abstract: Geopolitical risk is a key concern for the Euro Area, yet most available measures reflect a US perspective. This paper introduces a new indicator of geopolitical risk tailored to the Euro Area, based on newspaper coverage from local European sources. We show that shocks to this index have significant recessionary and inflationary effects in the Euro Area. Using a counterfactual exercise, we estimate the macroeconomic impact of the Russo-Ukrainian War on the Euro area economy in 2022, quantifying both output losses and inflationary pressures. We complement our analysis with two news-based measures of sanctions intensity and shortages, which we construct specifically for the Euro Area.

title: A Critical Analysis of Republic Act No. 9003: The Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000

detail.title: A Critical Analysis of Republic Act No. 9003: The Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000
detail.abstract: This paper examines the Republic Act No. 9003, also referred to as the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000, which was enacted to enhance a systematic and environmentally friendly solid waste management in the Philippines. The article discusses the most important provisions, strengths, and weaknesses of the law. Some of its numerous benefits include the fact that RA 9003 gives communities in the area more power, and it promotes the utilization of Materials Recovery Facilities (MRFs) and therefore shared accountability in waste management. Nonetheless, the law has been hampered by problems, including a lack of uniformity in enforcement, a lack of budget, and a lack of involvement of the people. The social, environmental, and economic consequences of the law are also discussed in the article (greater awareness of the population, a cleaner society, new recycling and composting). Lastly, effective suggestions are presented, and they include offering more support to local governments, better surveillance, greater education to the masses, and the involvement of the private sector. All in all, even though RA 9003 provides a comprehensive framework of sustainable waste management in the Philippines, its success will eventually be preconditioned on the consistent dedication of the government, municipalities, and residents.

title: Network Evidence on Credit-Risk Pricing in P2P Lending
affiliations: University of Twente, University of Twente, Zurich University of Applied Sciences and Cardiff University

detail.title: Network Evidence on Credit-Risk Pricing in P2P Lending

declarations.declarationOfInterest: We, the authors of this manuscript, declare that: • Disclosure of potential conflicts of interest: We have no conflict of interest that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this manuscript; • Research involving human participants and/or animals: Our study does not involve Human Participants and/or Animals; and • Informed consent: All authors are informed consent.
declarations.funderStatement: Lennart John Baals, Jörg Osterrieder, and Branka Hadji-Misheva acknowledge the financial support of the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF) under project number 100018E_205487.

detail.abstract: We study whether posted interest rates on a leading European P2P platform, Bondora, efficiently reflect borrower default risk. Using 22,000 primary-market loans from 2012-2022, we (i) extract key risk drivers via a Random Forest, (ii) build a weighted Gower similarity network, and (iii) partition loans into risk-homogeneous communities via the Louvain algorithm. Within each community we benchmark quoted rates against realised defaults ex-post and subsequently model ex-ante implied rates through gradient-boosting models (GBMs) that replicate the platform's pricing function. Our analysis uncovers substantial mispricing: 8.8% of loans exhibit rate deviations exceeding 100 basis points, creating annual wealth transfers of €102,000 between investors and borrowers in our sample alone. Mispricing peaks during the platform's 2015-2018 transition to risk-based pricing and diminishes thereafter, consistent with a platform learning effect. We find underpriced loans to concentrate among B-rated borrowers, while Crated borrowers face systematic overpricing despite similar risk profiles. Our network-analytical framework offers investors a tractable way to identify latent pricing inefficiencies and highlights how information frictions persist even in data-rich fintech markets.

title: The Finite-Sample Density of the Sufficient Statistic and Related Tests in a Gaussian Autoregression

detail.title: The Finite-Sample Density of the Sufficient Statistic and Related Tests in a Gaussian Autoregression
detail.abstract: A first-order Gaussian autoregressive model is considered. The exact finite-sample joint density of the minimal sufficient statistic is derived, for any value of the autoregressive parameter. This allows us to derive explicitly the exact density of the autocorrelation coefficient and its Studentized t-ratio, whose densities were available only in the asymptotic case and not for all values of the parameter and the statistic. This paper also demonstrates how to solve a general problem in statistical distribution theory (well beyond the specific case of autoregressive models), that of inverting confluent characteristic functions in multiple variables.

title: Antitrust Enforcement and Protected Speech: First Amendment Primer

detail.title: Antitrust Enforcement and Protected Speech: First Amendment Primer
detail.abstract: Recent state and federal initiatives have sought to use antitrust and consumer protection laws to regulate how online platforms moderate user content. Proposals from the Federal Trade Commission, the Department of Justice, and states all attempt to frame content moderation as an anticompetitive practice. This Article lays out the basics of First Amendment law and levels of scrutiny, and explains that the First Amendment protects platforms' editorial discretion as expressive activity. Drawing on Supreme Court precedent, including Moody v. NetChoice, this Article explains that government actions compelling or constraining the manner in which platforms organize or present speech constitute content-based and often viewpoint-based regulations, subject to strict scrutiny.

title: Institutions, Poverty Reduction, and Inclusive Growth in Nigeria: Rethinking the Poverty-Growth Nexus in a Weak Governance Environment

detail.title: Institutions, Poverty Reduction, and Inclusive Growth in Nigeria: Rethinking the Poverty-Growth Nexus in a Weak Governance Environment
detail.abstract: This study investigates the complex interplay between institutional quality, poverty reduction, and inclusive economic growth in Nigeria, with a focus on the structural and governance-related constraints that shape the poverty-growth nexus. Nigeria, despite being endowed with significant natural and human resources, continues to experience high poverty rates and persistent inequality, highlighting a disconnect between economic growth and social development outcomes. The research emphasizes that weak governance, institutional inefficiencies, and elite capture substantially impede the translation of growth into broad-based improvements in living standards. By integrating institutional economics frameworks with development theory, the study examines how formal institutions-such as legal systems, regulatory bodies, and fiscal governance structures-interact with informal governance mechanisms, including societal norms, political accountability, and trust, to influence poverty alleviation efforts. Employing econometric analyses on macroeconomic and social indicators, the study reveals that robust and credible institutions are crucial for ensuring that economic expansion benefits marginalized populations, promotes equitable income distribution, and strengthens resilience against socioeconomic shocks. The findings underscore the need to rethink traditional growth-centered strategies by placing institutional reforms at the core of poverty reduction policies and designing interventions that simultaneously enhance governance, social protection, and economic inclusion. This multidimensional perspective offers critical insights for policymakers, development practitioners, and scholars interested in fostering sustainable and inclusive development in resource-dependent and weakly governed economies.

title: Shahil’s Integrated Equilibrium Model — IEM™ v2.1

detail.title: Shahil’s Integrated Equilibrium Model — IEM™ v2.1
detail.abstract:
This paper introduces Shahil’s Integrated Equilibrium Model (IEM™ v2), a unified macroeconomic framework designed to maintain real-time stability between money, demand, supply, and buffer-stock dynamics. The model extends classical MV = PS logic by embedding adaptive buffers and automated release rules that coordinate monetary and real-sector decisions in a single system. IEM™ v2 formalizes how nominal liquidity (M·V), real demand (Qᵈ), production (Prod), and strategic buffers (B) should interact to keep effective demand aligned with deliverable supply, even under shocks.

The framework defines a closed-loop controller for buffer releases, a modified monetary adjustment rule, and sector-specific stability conditions. It incorporates perishables, durables, and service-capacity buffers with minimal spoilage and real-time monitoring. By integrating price signals, production cycles, and circulating liquidity, the model reduces inflation volatility, minimizes shortages, and improves policy coordination across agencies.

IEM™ v2 demonstrates that macro-stability can be achieved not by controlling a single variable, but by synchronizing money flow, supply capacity, and adaptive stock management. The paper concludes that the model offers a practical, scalable, and data-driven alternative to traditional demand–supply management, suitable for both emerging and advanced economies.

title: Varying Levels of Lateral Acceleration Supplied on Interchange Loops with No Speed Signs for Guidance

detail.title: Varying Levels of Lateral Acceleration Supplied on Interchange Loops with No Speed Signs for Guidance
detail.abstract: Highway interchanges should not be left ''unattended'' when it comes to signage, but in many countries such key locations lack adequate speed limit signs. Therefore, drivers, who normally expect ''accustomed'' lateral acceleration levels when negotiating the loops of interchanges, have to choose correct speeds on their own. The paper reveals the extent of this problem using ball-bank data collected from four Turkish cloverleaf interchanges. Three criteria are introduced: 1) first maximum, 2) rate of change of radial acceleration, and 3) average riding comfort along the loops. The following features are scrutinized: in criterion 1, the first maximum ball-bank reading for each loop against its corresponding speed; in criterion 2, how quickly the lateral acceleration develops as the test vehicle enters and exits a loop; and in criterion 3, the average values of ball-bank readings as the test vehicle travels along the loops. To maintain the same level of lateral comfort, the test vehicle had to experience about 6 km/h speed variation among the loops of the same interchange, and more than 15 km/h speed variation among the interchanges studied, as far as criterion 1 is concerned. In relation to criterion 2, the test vehicle underwent a faster ball-bank differential when entering a loop than it did when exiting. With regard to criterion 3, about 4 km/h speed variation among the loops of the same interchange and nearly 16 km/h speed variation among the interchanges studied were recorded. The methodology developed in this paper can easily be adapted for similar objectives to study the loops of interchanges in other countries.

title: The Impact of Expectation Confirmation Factors on Customer Satisfaction in E-Commerce - An Insight on Consumer Behavior in Vietnam

detail.title: The Impact of Expectation Confirmation Factors on Customer Satisfaction in E-Commerce - An Insight on Consumer Behavior in Vietnam
detail.abstract: In the context of e-commerce, only a minority of businesses find success in this field. The larger proportion fails partly due to dissatisfied customers as satisfaction has been linked to build loyalty and encourage repurchase behaviour among customers. This study aims to assess the relationship between different factors of expectation confirmation and customer satisfaction, addressing gaps in the existing literature related to this topic as the majority of them were only conducted in developed countries and examined confirmation in a general way. A survey was used to collect data from online shoppers in Vietnam. The study used quantitative correlational research to determine the relationship between the variables. The result showed positive correlation between each of the confirmation factors-Perceived Similarity Confirmation (PSC), Perceived Quality Confirmation (PQC), Perceived Value Confirmation (PVC), and customer Satisfaction (SAT). Among them, the most influential finding was the relationship between PSC and SAT as PSC has not been used as a construct in prior studies. The findings suggested that business should focus on similarity, quality and value to ensure satisfaction among customers. Further research should employ a larger sample size with more evenly distributed demographics groups to improve the generalizability of the findings.

title: Breaking the Unholy Alliance: A Blueprint for Hope

detail.title: Breaking the Unholy Alliance: A Blueprint for Hope

declarations.declarationOfInterest: none

detail.abstract: This work completes the Bocchinfuso III Canon by offering a comprehensive blueprint for stabilizing a society emerging from a decade of emotionalized governance, narrative dominance, and institutional fragility. While earlier volumes diagnosed the convergence of media incentives, psychological drift, institutional fear, and generational overexposure to crisis narratives, Breaking the Unholy Alliance: A Blueprint for Hope provides the structural and civic framework necessary for recovery. Drawing upon interdisciplinary insights from political psychology, institutional sociology, media studies, and generational development, the book outlines five core responsibilities—cognitive sovereignty, institutional transparency, generational stewardship, proportionality, and civic humility—each treated not as moral prescriptions but as systems-level stabilizers required for long-term social equilibrium. The analysis demonstrates that emotional monopolies collapse not through opposition but through the restoration of calm, clarity, and distributed responsibility. This blueprint proposes a post-narrative future in which individuals reclaim interpretive independence, institutions rebuild trust through transparency rather than performance, and emerging generations inherit healthier psychological environments. The work positions hope not as sentiment, but as design: the outcome of disciplined emotional posture, structural realism, and the rediscovery of shared reality.
