detail.abstract: The prevailing mindset in crypto is still anchored in fiat thinking: evaluating progress in dollars rather than in quantity accumulation of core assets (ETH/BTC). This paper argues that fiat-denominated thinking is structurally limiting and psychologically destructive. It biases the investor toward shortterm valuation anxiety rather than long-horizon quantity compounding. This paper offers a systematic framework—Systematic Token Accumulation and Cryptocurrency Kit (STACK)—designed to: 1. Escape fiat-denominated evaluation. 2. Optimize token quantity, not portfolio dollar value. 3. Deploy liquidity according to cyclical and structural signals instead of prediction. 4. Use rotations into and out of altcoins strategically to reduce ETH cost basis over time. Core Thesis: Richness is not the number of dollars you have. Richness is ownership of scarce assets that the system cannot print. The sovereign investor accumulates units, not prices.

title: From Economy to Post-Economy: The Semantic Architecture of Ethical Value

detail.title: From Economy to Post-Economy: The Semantic Architecture of Ethical Value
detail.abstract: This paper develops the theory of a Post-Economy of Ethical Semantics, a paradigm in which value emerges not through exchange or scarcity but through meaning, dignity, and semantic coherence. Building on earlier work on blockchain-mediated emotional economies, the study shows that attempts to commodify affect reveal a deeper contradiction: moral and relational phenomena lose their ethical character when expressed as tokens. The post-economic framework therefore reconceives value as a relational property grounded in recognition, provenance, and distributed responsibility. Central to this model is the Ethical Governance Layer (EGL), a hybrid human-machine infrastructure in which computational systems ensure transparency and logical consistency, while human agents retain interpretative and moral authority. Through ontologies, provenance graphs, and distributed ledgers, the EGL renders ethical deliberation traceable without reducing it to computation. By reframing political economy as the organisation of meaning rather than goods, the post-economic model provides a foundation for a non-commodified yet operational account of dignity. The paper concludes by outlining future research on semantic legitimacy, ethical risk, and prototype implementations of the EGL.

title: Leaning with Prices or Quantities? Optimal Monetary-Macroprudential Policy under Bubble Uncertainty

detail.title: Leaning with Prices or Quantities? Optimal Monetary-Macroprudential Policy under Bubble Uncertainty
detail.abstract: Central banks confront asset-price booms in which rising prices and credit may reflect improved fundamentals or speculative disagreement, and real-time diagnosis is imperfect. We develop a tractable two-period model with heterogeneous valuations and selective participation in which the policymaker chooses between the policy rate-a price instrument that shifts the allin borrowing cost-and a macroprudential cap on aggregate exposure-a quantity instrument. Because observed price indices are built from realized trades, they reflect the average valuation of transactors rather than the unconditional mean payoff. In tail-driven booms, both higher fundamentals and higher disagreement raise participation, credit, and transaction-based prices, so the directional co-movement of (P, Q) is not by itself diagnostic of the underlying boom driver. Moreover, tightening via the policy rate screens out marginal participants and can mechanically raise a transaction-based price index even as activity and credit fall. A cap reduces exposure without this compositional distortion and provides insurance when distress losses are convex in aggregate credit due to fire-sale spillovers and balance-sheet stress. Under a simple two-regime specification for disagreement, we derive a transparent assignment rule: quantity tools are preferred when boom identification is noisy and amplification is severe, whereas the policy rate is preferred when signals are informative or amplification is mild. A lightweight U.S. housing illustration using monthly monetary-policy surprises and local projections documents early quantity responses to tightening and a boom-contingent divergence between a median transaction-price statistic and a constant-quality index.

title: Competition in Pricing Algorithms: Stability, Exploration, and Supracompetitive Outcomes
affiliations: Singapore Management University - Lee Kong Chian School of Business and Singapore Management University - Lee Kong Chian School of Business

detail.title: Competition in Pricing Algorithms: Stability, Exploration, and Supracompetitive Outcomes
detail.abstract: Antitrust regulators are increasingly concerned that rms employing advanced reinforcement learning techniques may "learn to collude". But is complex articial intelligence, such as Q-learning algorithms or pricing LLMs, necessary to sustain supracompetitive prices? We argue that the barrier to collusion is far lower. We investigate a dynamic setting where rms employ a widely adopted form of misspecied demand model that ignores competitive interactions. Using tools from Stochastic Approximation and Lyapunov Analysis, we analyze the global stability of this dynamic system. We derive a Stability Condition, which identies a tension between the stabilizing force of demand learning and the destabilizing feedback loops induced by misspecication. We provide insights into how this tension may lead to elevated (supracompetitive) prices that mimic collusion. Our analysis uncovers three distinct non-collusive mechanisms that drive prices above competitive levels: (i) correlated exploration or common market shocks mask signals related to competition, which cause the market to mimic collusive outcomes without explicit communication between the rms; (ii) asymmetric information and algorithmic speed may allow a fast-reacting rm to exploit Omitted Variable Bias, strategically inducing its competitor to underestimate price elasticity; (iii) when the stability condition is violated, due to high market coupling or insucient price experimentation, destabilizing feedback loops drive the system toward outcomes where rms misperceive demand as inelastic. Taken together, our study shows that supracompetitive prices can emerge as a statistical artifact of learning under a misspecied model, complementing prior work that attributes such outcomes to more sophisticated forward-looking mechanisms, such as reward-and-punishment schemes. This underscores the need for regulators to scrutinize algorithmic design choices that could inadvertently lead to supracompetitive pricing.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Intellectual Property Rights: Comparative Transnational Policy Analysis

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence and Intellectual Property Rights: Comparative Transnational Policy Analysis

publicationDetails.detailsText: Journal of University Institute of Legal Studies, Volume 19, No. 1. Pp. 182-208

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence's rapid integration with intellectual property rights necessitates a detailed assessment of its impact. This is especially critical for trade secrets, copyrights and patents. The significance of this study lies in addressing the lacunae within existing laws. India lacks AI-specific provisions. This results in doctrinal inconsistencies and enforcement inefficacies. Global institutions have initiated discourse on AI-related IPR protections but international harmonization remains nascent. This necessitates a deeper inquiry into jurisdictional divergences and regulatory constraints. This research identifies critical gaps in the adaptability of Indian IP laws to AI-generated or AI-assisted outputs. Trade secret protection remains inadequate against AI-driven threats. Standardized inventorship criteria remain absent. This study employs a doctrinal and comparative legal methodology. It scrutinizes legislative texts and examines judicial precedents. It evaluates policy instruments across India, the United States, the United Kingdom, and the European Union. It incorporates insights from international organizations. Preliminary findings indicate fundamental shortcomings. India's reliance on conventional contract law results in a fragmented trade secret regime. AI-driven innovations remain vulnerable. Section 3(k) of the Indian Patents Act impedes the patenting of AI-generated inventions. Copyright frameworks exhibit jurisdictional variances in authorship attribution. This study underscores the necessity for a harmonized legal taxonomy that accommodates AI’s transformative role. Innovation incentives and ethical considerations must be preserved. India's National AI Strategy (2024) signals incremental progress; however, legislative clarity remains imperative.  This research contributes to the ongoing global discourse by proposing a robust legal architecture that integrates AI-specific IP protections. It ensures resilience against emergent challenges while fostering equitable innovation. The promising results derived from this analysis underscore the urgency of recalibrating India's IP jurisprudence. Alignment with global advancements remains essential.

The research was conducted in accordance with the ethical principles outlined in the Declaration of Helsinki and the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) National Ethical Guidelines for Biomedical and Health Research Involving Human Participants (2017). detail.abstract: Quality of Work Life (QWL) has emerged as a critical dimension of employee wellbeing and organizational sustainability (Sirgy et al., 2001; Walton, 1973). In industrial clusters such as Mandideep, workplace infrastructure and environmental conditions significantly shape workers' perceptions of safety, comfort, and job satisfaction. This study examines how infrastructural facilities-including lighting, ventilation, ergonomic furniture, sanitation, and workspace design-along with environmental factors such as noise, heat, pollution, and cleanliness influence QWL among industrial workers. Primary data were collected from 320 respondents across manufacturing units in Mandideep Industrial Area, supported by secondary insights from census reports, industrial records, and safety audits. The findings reveal substantial infrastructural deficits and environmental stressors that adversely affect workers' physical and psychological comfort, thereby diminishing overall QWL. The study offers evidence-based recommendations for improving workplace design, safety management, and environmental compliance.

title: Bigger than we thought: Methodological choices and the magnitude of Child Penalties in Chile
affiliations: , , University of Chile - Department of Economics and University College London - UCL Social Research Institute

detail.title: Bigger than we thought: Methodological choices and the magnitude of Child Penalties in Chile
detail.abstract: This paper re-examines the role of motherhood in shaping gender gaps in labor market outcomes in Chile. Using all available waves of the Social Protection Survey (EPS, 2002–2024), we construct a longitudinal panel tracking individuals before and after the birth of their first child, and estimate dynamic treatment effects via event-study models with age and time fixed effects. We document and overcome a methodological problem in the existing literature: the expansion of retrospective employment spells into repeated monthly observations, which mechanically introduces smoothing and inflates precision. By relying exclusively on information recorded contemporaneously at the interview date, we provide cleaner and more credible estimates of child penalties. Our results reveal substantially larger and more persistent penalties than previously reported. Maternal employment declines by about 40% immediately after birth, and a 55% motherhood penalty remains 15 years later, while fathers’ participation remains stable. Earnings drop even more sharply, driven mainly by exits from employment. Penalties are strongly heterogeneous: they are largest for partnered mothers, those above age 30 at childbirth, and those who were primary earners prior to birth. These findings underscore the centrality of motherhood in perpetuating gender gaps and highlight the importance of policies improving childcare access and work–family compatibility in Chile.

title: Antitrust Boundary Pushing Without Overreach

detail.title: Antitrust Boundary Pushing Without Overreach
detail.abstract: Calls to “democratize” antitrust have intensified as enforcers seek to reverse underenforcement and address platform, labor-market, and innovation harms. This paper argues that plebiscitary participation is impractical and mismatched to antitrust’s institutional design. U.S. antitrust evolves through a common-law engine: agencies and litigants test boundaries; courts refine standards through adjudication; and Congress, state enforcers, and private plaintiffs provide oversight and enforcement. Within that architecture, boundary pushing is legitimate—and often necessary—when it is candid about novelty, anchored in necessity and proportionality, and supported by evidence that can survive appellate review. The paper distinguishes incremental “edge testing” from doctrinal “leaps,” highlights the risk of portfolio overreach when too many theories are pursued at once, and offers seven guardrails: own the novelty; justify necessity; build portable records; design for scrutiny; contain uncertainty; sequence priorities; and engage the public without surrendering expertise. It offers judges and practitioners a disciplined framework for antitrust boundary pushing.

title: Seeking Gamma: Lessons from the Meme Frenzy
affiliations: West Virginia University, Department of Finance, Wayne State University - Mike Ilitch School of Business and Boise State University - College of Business and Economics

detail.title: Seeking Gamma: Lessons from the Meme Frenzy
detail.abstract: There has been substantial debate about the existence and impact of a gamma squeeze during the GameStop price surge in January 2021. We provide novel empirical evidence confirming that a gamma squeeze indeed occurred and suggest that this squeeze started earlier than previously documented, in the Fall of 2020. We also identify other gamma squeeze episodes across a broader set of meme stocks during the same time period. Extending our analysis beyond meme stocks to all U.S. stocks, we systematically identify 669 potential gamma squeeze events from 2019 to 2023. These gamma squeezes result in economically significant price impacts, generating an average cumulative abnormal return of 5.13% in the month following their initiation. Our findings offer valuable insights for researchers, regulators, and market participants.

title: Moderation is the Cure to the Crisis in Antitrust Expertise

detail.title: Moderation is the Cure to the Crisis in Antitrust Expertise
detail.abstract: After decades of relative obscurity, antitrust reentered the public square roughly a decade ago, as trust in expertise was waning. This essay argues that the resulting “crisis of expertise” in competition policy is driven by motivated reasoning, special interest influence, and populist distrust—forces that reward imprecise and sometimes misleading narratives. On one side, Neo-Brandeisian advocates portray antitrust as a remedy for broad social and economic ills; on the other, enforcement skeptics characterize modern antitrust enforcement as anti-business ideology. The essay shows how these camps blur the boundary between expertise and advocacy and how, under current conditions, competition in the “marketplace of ideas” can amplify error rather than correct it. It further contends that enforcers sometimes deepen the problem by privileging intuitive but doctrinally strained arguments that resonate with populist sensibilities over rigorous economic reasoning and careful evidentiary claims. The prescription is technocratic moderation: disciplined attention to doctrine, economics, and tradeoffs; methodological and evidentiary rigor; and agency leadership that reinforces courts’ limited antitrust mandate. The payoff is a more credible and administrable antitrust law.
